Held, yes [Para 20] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company had earned revenue from information technology/BPO related services and sales from infra activities, due to non-availability of reliable segmental data, selected company could not be considered to be comparable to assessee, rendering ITE services  TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company earned income from data analytics services and process solutions, it could not be compared with assessee for benchmarking international transaction pertaining to provision of ITeS services  TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company operated in 3 segments and had un-allocable expenses which rendered its financial information relating to aforesaid 3 segments unreliable, said company could not be considered to be comparable  TRANSFER PRICING : Where TPO rejected a company as a comparable on basis that it had negative net worth, but it was found that TPO had computed net worth of company incorrectly and for year under consideration, correct net worth of company was not negative, said company could be compared with assessee for benchmarking international transaction pertaining to provision of ITeS services  TRANSFER PRICING : Where entire revenue of company from services was from domestic contracts, whereas assessee's entire earnings was from export of services, then said company could not be considered to be functionally comparable to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company was proposed to be considered as a comparable by TPO but data pertaining to said company was not provided to assessee by TPO, in absence of data being available in public domain, selected company cannot be considered as comparable to assessee

Section  92C,  read with section  92CA,  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Transfer Pricing  -  Computation of Arm’s length price  (Adjustments - Segmentation) - Assessment year  2018-19  - Assessee, engaged in testing, inspection and certification (TIC) services to third-party customers in India and to AEs, also provided ITES support and shared services to AEs - For transfer pricing, it prepared segmental accounts showing AE margins of about 15% in ITES, shared services and certification segments, a 4% margin in non-AE certification services, an overall margin of about 6%, and ITES revenue of about Rs. 4.53 crores out of total revenue of about Rs. 124.81 crores (non-AE certification about Rs. 97.40 crores; AE certification about Rs. 15.09 crores; shared services about Rs. 7.79 crores) - In its TPSR, it benchmarked ITES transactions of about Rs. 4.5 crores under TNMM using OP/OC with a margin of 15% - On reference, TPO grouped TIC, shared services and ITES together as ITES, rejected assessee's segmental results stating that HR, finance, operations, legal and admin costs were not allocated to AEs, computed a consolidated margin of 4.44%, rejected TPSR and proposed a TP adjustment of about Rs. 26.18 crores - Whether since for earlier AYs TIC and ITES services were benchmarked separately, as TIC services and ITES services did not share same FAR, and TP Order did not explain why TIC and ITES services were being grouped together, combining TIC and ITES services for benchmarking was not justified - Held, yes [Para 24] [In favour of assessee]

V.Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Assessee had entered into an agreement with its AE for providing IT back office support services - Whether when segmental information for each stream of income were not available and it became difficult to benchmark profit margin of comparable, matter should be remanded back - Held, yes - Whether where material facts were different and comparable had been selected on some incorrect analysis in earlier year or at time of TP study, then definitely there cannot be any estoppel for objecting to for its A exclusion - Held, yes - Whether a company be excluded from comparability analysis where due to its exceptional performance during year, it had been chosen as best KPO company and it had also outsourced its substantial work to third party - Held, yes - Whether where comparable company was requested by assessee for inclusion before DRP by way of detailed submissions, but DRP did not provide its comments on this comparable, matter should be reconsidered afresh - Held, yes [Paras 10-20][Partly in favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustration) - Assessment year 2011-12 - Assessee provided IT enbled services in infrastructure development and testing, system and performance operations management and support - Whether a company providing consultancy business solution and testing and high end BPO services, in absence of segmental data was incomparable - Held, yes - Whether a company engaged in KPO services in healthcare sector could not be selected as comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Para 13] [In favour of assessee]IT/ILT: A company providing consultancy business solution and testing, and high end BPO services, in absence of segmental data, was incomparable to ITES provider

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee-company was rendering IT enabled services to its AE - Whether a company which outsourced major portion of its work to third party vendors, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether companies providing high end KPO services in field of payroll, finance, accounting, structural engineering and consulting services etc., were not acceptable as comparables on account of functional difference - Held, yes - Whether company engaged in software development services was functionally different and, thus, not acceptable as comparable - Held, yes - Whether company which was earning revenue from software development services as well as sale of software products about which segmental information was not available, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Para 10] [In favour of assessee]

II.Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparable - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Assessee was a captive service provider to its AE providing software development services - Whether where assessee sought exclusion of a comparable on ground that it was outsourcing its services; it was also engaged in development of products with no segmental data available and that it was expending around 1 per cent of its total income on RD activities, however said comparable had not been contested by assessee before TPO as well as DRP, matter was to be remanded back for adjudication afresh - Held, yes [Para 18][Matter remanded]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arms length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company which has outsourced most of its work to third party can be compared to a company carrying out work by itself - Held, no - Whether a company is not a comparable for having extraordinary circumstances, i.e., amalgamation - Held, yes - Whether where a comparable company is operating in a different business model than that of assessee, it should be excluded from comparable list - Held, yes - Whether a company indulged in high skill IT services is not comparable to routine IT Enabled services - Held, yes [Para 9] [In favour of assessee]IT/ILT : A company which has outsourced most of its work to third party cannot be compared to a company carrying out work by itself

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - BPO/Call centre) - Assessment year 2011-12 - Assessee was low end BPO services provider - Whether a company rendering high end engineering design services could not be compared with assessee - Held, yes [Para 12] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : A company rendering high end engineering design services could not be compared with assessee, a low end BPO services provider  TRANSFER PRICING : Where a company's BPO segment failed revenue filter of more than 75 per cent applied by TPO, same was incomparable  TRANSFER PRICING : Where a company's software services segment was clubbed with Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) segment and there was no break-up between revenue generated from said segments, this company was incomparable to assessee engaged in providing ITES only

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2004-05 - Whether since assessee has itself selected company as a comparable company in its TP study and selected company was also in ITES services which could be separated or segmented, like in assessee's case also could not be verified therefore, comparability of selected company is required to be reexamined by TPO - Held, yes [Para 16.5] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee has itself selected company as a comparable company in its TP study and selected company was also in ITES services which could be separated or segmented, like in assessee's case also could not be verified therefore, comparability of selected company is required to be re-examined by TPO  TRANSFER PRICING : Both loss making unit and high profit making unit cannot be eliminated from comparables unless, there are specific reasons for eliminating same which is other than general reason that comparable has incurred loss or made abnormal profits  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who has developed unique software from which it would derive substantial benefits advantages when compared with assessee which is undertaking pure call centre services therefore, company cannot be held as comparable to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who is outsourcing most of its work cannot be held comparable to assessee who was carrying out work by itself  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who having influence of 'Wipro' brand and also having its unique intangibles cannot be held comparable to captive service provider such as assessee

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of Arm's Length Price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Assessee-company was engaged in two business segments, namely, software development services as a service provider for mobile phones and ITES segment which included call centre and other allied support services - Whether where services rendered by TCS E-serve were high end KPO services but it was not brought out as to which of these were services that would come under technical services while TPO held all services rendered by assessee to be BPO services without any proper analysis, it would be appropriate to remand matter of comparability of this company - Held, yes [Para 9.3.1][Matter remanded]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee-company was engaged in rendering software development services and IT enabled services to its AE - Whether where a company had outsourced considerable portion of its ITES business, it could not be compared to assessee carrying out entire operation by itself - Held, yes - Whether a company mainly engaged in providing high end services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise in field of data analytics and data process solutions was not comparable to assessee - Held,yes [Paras 22 and 23] [In favour of assessee/Matter remanded]

I.Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables-Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether in case of assessee rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which significantly outsourced its activities, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Para 10] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT-I: In case of assessee, rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which significantly outsourced its activities, could not be accepted as comparable  IT/ILT-II: While determining ALP suitable adjustments can be made not only in margins of comparables but also in margins of tested party  IT/ILT-III: In case of assessee rendering IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE, a company having turnover and brand value and a company providing KPO services, could not be accepted as comparables

IV.Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2011-12 Assessee was engaged in providing information technology enabled services (ITeS) to its AEs - Whether a company which had outsourced its contract for services would not be comparable to assessee which operate through its own human resources - Held, yes [Para 34][In favour of assessee]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Adjustment - Operating expenses) - Assessment year 2010-11 - Assessee was engaged in business of providing IT enabled services to its AEs - TPO did not agree with various filters used by assessee in its TP study and selected certain new comparables - TPO while calculating PLI of comparables had taken miscellaneous income as operating in nature -Assessee submitted that miscellaneous income should be non-operating in absence of details and nature of miscellaneous income received by comparables - However, TPO/Assessing Officer had not made any effort to look into this aspect - Whether therefore, matter was to be remanded back to TPO/Assessing Officer for adjudication afresh - Held, yes [Para 24] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT : Matter remanded to TPO/Assessing Officer to decide whether in absence of details and nature of miscellaneous income received by comparables, miscellaneous income could have been taken to be operating in nature  IT/ILT : Where TPO while calculating PLI of comparables had himself accepted that donation and provision for doubtful debt was non-operating, same was to be applied while calculating PLI of assessee also  IT/ILT : Matter remanded to TPO/Assessing Officer to verify evidences/bills/details/correspondence relating to expenditure incurred on non-operational unit of assessee and to decide whether they were operating/non-operating expenses  IT/ILT : Company engaged in digital library and print on demand in case of which segmental details were not available would not be comparable to company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs  IT/ILT : Company engaged in rendering software development and engineering design services would not be comparable to company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs  IT/ILT : A giant company having huge asset base, brand value, goodwill and presence in global market and being a full fledged risk bearing service provider having significant R  D activities would not be comparable to IT enabled service provider  IT/ILT : Company engaged in healthcare receivables cycle management in which case extraordinary events of amalgamation and acquisition had taken place during relevant year, however, no segmental details were available, would not be comparable to company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs  IT/ILT : A company engaged in data analytics and financial services, in which extraordinary event of acquisition had taken place during year, would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : A company in which an extraordinary event of acquisition of a group during relevant year had taken place would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : Company engaged in providing geographical information services comprising photogrammetric, remote sensing cartonography, data conversion, related computer based services and other related services being functionally different would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : Where ITES segment of a company was similar to that of assessee-company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs, but there was discrepancy in annual report and in information gathered under section 133(6), said company could not have been taken as comparable  IT/ILT : Company engaged in product development and for which no segmental data was available, would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : Where ITES activities of a company included data centre management services, end user computing services, managed security services, which were not functionally similar to that of assessee company providing IT enabled services to its AE, said company had to be excluded from final list of comparables

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company providing high-level services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise and being a leading provider of KPO services would not be functionally comparable to assessee engaged in providing low-end ITES enabled call centre services to its AE - Held, yes - Whether assessee-company having a business model where services were rendered by employing own employees and using one's own infrastructure would have a different cost structure as compared to a business model where services were outsourced and hence would not be comparable - Held, yes - Whether where DRP had omitted to record any finding regarding comparability of a company, matter required readjudication - Held, yes - Whether assessee would be permitted to raise objections against a comparable first time before Tribunal, but adjudication on inclusion/exclusion of this company from final list of comparables was to be restored to file of TPO - Held, yes [Para 16] [In favour of assessee/Matter remanded]IT/ILT: Company providing high-level services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise and being a leading provider of KPO services would not be functionally comparable to assessee, a BPO engaged in providing low-end ITES enabled call centre services to its AE

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparable, factor to determine - Segmental results) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company had earned revenue from information technology/BPO related services and sales from infra activities, but due to non-availability of reliable segmental data, said company could not be considered to be comparable to assessee rendering ITE services - Held, yes [Para 20] [In favour of assessee]  II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITeS)) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company was KPO company and earned revenue from data analytics services and process solutions, it could not be compared with assessee rendering ITE services - Held, yes [Para 24] [In favour of assessee]  III. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (comparability factors - Segmental result) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company operated in 3 segments and had un-allocable expenses which rendered its financial information relating to aforesaid 3 segments unreliable, said company could not be considered to be comparable - Held, yes [Para 27] [In favour of assessee]  IV. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Others) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where TPO rejected a company as a comparable on basis that it had negative net worth but it was found that TPO had computed net worth of company incorrectly and for year under consideration, correct net worth of company was not negative, said company could be compared with assessee rendering ITeS - Held, yes [Para 30] [In favour of assessee]  V. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Export filter) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where entire revenue of selected company was from domestic contracts, whereas assessee's entire earnings was from export of business support services, said company could not be considered to be functionally comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Para 33] [In favour of assessee]  VI. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Data in public domain) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company was proposed to be considered as a comparable by TPO but data pertaining to this company was not provided to assessee by TPO, in absence of data being available in public domain, selected company could not be considered as comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Para 36] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - ITES) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether company deriving significant portion of its receipts from outsourcing translation work and making payment of about Rs. 3 crores cannot be held good comparable with assessee engaged in ITES segment and needs to be excluded - Held, yes [Para 13] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : A company deriving significant portion of its receipts from outsourcing translation work and making payment of about Rs. 3 crores cannot be held good comparable with assessee engaged in ITES segment and needs to be excluded  TRANSFER PRICING : When missing of details relating to capacity underutilization adjustment resulted in observation of TPO that TP study of assessee has not made any such adjustment, then issue should be remanded to file of Assessing Officer/TPO for considering capacity underutilization adjustment in light of TP study and by requiring details, if any, from assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company engaged in relative position of things on earth's surface which include 3D mapping, Navigation maps, image processing, Cadastral mapping etc. cannot be compared with assessee providing services in ITES segment

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee rendered ITES to its AE - Whether company engaged in providing engineering design service which is a high end service in nature of KPO,cannot be treated as comparable - Held, yes - Whether company which had outsourced its ITES to third party vendors was incomparable - Held, yes - Whether since extraordinary event had impacted profitability of comparable company, it should be excluded from comparable list - Held, yes - Whether engineering design services could not be compared to IT enabled services - Held, yes [Paras 53 to 67][Matter remanded]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE as captive service provider, a company which outsourced major portion of its work, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Para 15.3.2] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Employees Cost) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where assessee was rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which outsourced major portion of its work to third parties and thereby followed a different business model, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Para 11] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which outsourced major portion of its work to third parties and thereby followed a different business model, could not be accepted as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was rendering ITES services to its AE, a company having unreliable financial data, was not acceptable as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING: Where TPO made addition to assessee's ALP in respect of interest on loan availed from AE, in view of fact that computation of interest by TPO on basis of RBI ECB rate was flawed since interest was paid by assessee to AEs located in foreign countries, impugned addition was to be deleted

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITES)) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Assessee-company was engaged in providing Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) to its Associated Enterprises (AEs) - TPO selected certain companies as comparable to assessee - It was found that Tribunal in case of Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT in [2018] 97 taxmann.com 2 (Banglore-Trib.) had remanded matter as regards said comparables for examination and verification of issues raised by assessee of functional comparability and employees cost filter of 25 per cent at segmental level - Whether, in view of aforesaid, issue of comparability of said companies was to be remanded back to TPO for examination - Held, yes [Para 6.3.2] [Matter remanded]TRANSFER PRICING: In view of Tribunal's decision in Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT in [2018] 97 taxmann.com 2 (Banglore-Trib.) issue of comparability of companies selected by TPO was to be remanded for examination and verification of issues raised by assessee of functional comparability and employees cost filter of 25 per cent at segmental level  TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was providing Information Technology Enabled Services to its AEs, a company having huge brand value was to be excluded from list of comaprables  TRANSFER PRICING: A company which had extraordinary events happened in relevant year under consideration such as acquisition of an Australian company which had effect on its profits was to be excluded from list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING: Where a company had 3 segments and benchmarking had been done only with one segment and it was not clear, how much of RPT expenses pertained to each of segments, matter was to be remanded  TRANSFER PRICING: Where a company was Knowledge Process Outsourcing (KPO) services provider but it was not determined which of these services came under technical services while assessee was having Information Technology Enabled Service segment which was held by TPO as Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) without any analysis, matter was to be remanded  TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee's consideration that a company had failed employee cost filter of 25 per cent had not been examined either by TPO or by assessee at segmental level and similar was position with regard to volatility of profits/peculiarity of economic circumstances, matter was to be remanded  TRANSFER PRICING: A company which was predominantly a Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) company, was comparable to assessee providing Information Technology Enabled Services to its AEs  TRANSFER PRICING: Where DRP excluded a company from set of comparables, however, it was found that said company had only one segment, namely, Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) segment which was functionally comparable to assessee providing ITES services, in view of aforesaid, matter was to be restored to TPO for examining afresh comparability of said company

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Segmental result) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Whether a company providing medical transcription, medical coding services and application, development and customization services and also engaged in business of developing software products in respect of which segmental data was not available cannot be held comparable to assessee providing ITES services to its AEs - Held, yes [Para 10] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : A company providing medical transcription, medical coding services and application, development and customization services and also engaged in business of developing software products in respect of which segmental data was not available cannot be held comparable to assessee providing ITES services to its AEs  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who was data analytics KPO service provider and has also acquired another UK based company providing different services, viz., Travel and hospitality cannot be compared to BPO or an IT offshore company such as assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who was KPO providing structural engineering services wherein during year under consideration, extraordinary events such as amalgamation and demerger have taken place cannot be held comparable to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company whose performance of Engineering Design Services is regarded as providing high end services among BPO which requires high skill cannot be held comparable to assessee providing routine low end ITES functions

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparable and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2010-11 - Assessee-company was engaged in provision of software development services to its AE - Whether a company engaged in both software development and ITES in absence of segmental data was not comparable to assessee - Held, yes - Whether fluctuating profits could not be a reason to exclude companies unless business profile was entirely different - Held, yes - Whether where assessee objected to a company on ground that it outsourced its business, there was presence of intangible assets and also said company had very high turnover, Assessing Officer/TPO not having examined matter, it was to be remitted back for fresh adjudication by Assessing Officer/TPO to see whether functional dissimilarity and high turnover had application to facts of case of assessee-company - Held, yes [Partly in favour of assessee]IT/ILT: Company engaged in both software development and ITES in absence of segmental data is not comparable to company engaged only in software development services  IT/ILT: Where bad debts and provision for bad and doubtful debts were part of operating expenses, TPO was to be directed to re-compute margins of comparable companies by including them for purpose of computing profit and loss of comparable companies  IT/ILT: There is no need for making any negative working capital adjustment when assessee does not bear any working capital risk

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of Arm's Length Price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - ITES v. Software development) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Assessee-company was engaged in two business segments, namely, software development services as a service provider for mobile phones and ITES segment which included call centre and other allied support services - Comparable company had four segments viz., Repro, Label Printing, Offset Printing and Pre-press BPO - Assessee raised issue of functional comparability and employees cost filter of 25 per cent at segmental level - Whether issue of comparability of this company was to be remanded back to file of TPO for examination - Held, yes [Para 6.3.1] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT: Where assessee had business in two segments and in respect of selection of comparable companies for ITES segment, issue of functional comparability and employee cost filter was raised but same was not ascertained, matter was to be remanded  IT/ILT: Company which had high brand value and in which extraordinary event of acquisition of foreign company took place, was to be excluded  IT/ILT: Where for a company, it was not determined how much RPT pertained to medical transcription so as to determine its comparability with assessee-ITES provider, matter was to be remanded  IT/ILT: Where selected company was high end KPO services provider but it was not determined which of these services came under technical services while assessee was having ITES segment which was held by TPO as BPO, matter was to be remanded

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITES)) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Assessee-company was engaged in providing Information Technology Enabled Services to its Associated Enterprises (AEs) - DRP suo moto excluded a company from set of comparables - It was found that under head 'Segmental Reporting' said company had only one segment, namely, Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) segment - Total sales/turnover was also entirely from BPO activities - Further, it was found that effect of 'other income' on margin of company had not been examined - Whether, in view of aforesaid factual matrix, matter was to be restored to TPO for examining afresh comparability of said company - Held, yes [Para 8.3.2] [Matter remanded]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Whether a company who was outsourcing all its activities cannot be regarded as comparable with assessee engaged on its own in rendering ITeS services - Held, yes [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : A company outsourcing all its activities cannot be regarded as comparable with assessee engaged on its own in rendering ITeS services   TRANSFER PRICING : A company having employee cost of only 11.45 per cent of its revenue cannot be held comparable to assessee as employee cost should be at least 25 per cent of revenue to regard company as comparable with ITeS provider like assessee

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - ITES) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether company deriving significant portion of its receipts from outsourcing translation work and making payment of about Rs. 3 crores cannot be held good comparable with assessee engaged in ITES segment and needs to be excluded - Held, yes [Para 13] [In favour of assessee]  II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Adjustments - Capacity utilization) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Assessee claim for adjustment of low capacity utilization for ideal capacity, in TP study which missed attention of TPO in TP study previously - However, revenue claimed that observations of TPO that certain details and data in support of claim of assessee were required and assessee should be directed to produce such details before Assessing Officer/TPO - Whether when missing of details relating to capacity underutilization adjustment resulted in observation of TPO that TP study of assessee has not made any such adjustment, then issue should be remanded to file of Assessing Officer/TPO for considering capacity underutilization adjustment in light of TP study and by requiring details, if any, from assessee - Held, yes [Para 14] [In favour of assessee]  III. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company engaged in relative position of things on earth's surface which include 3D mapping, Navigation maps, image processing, Cadastral mapping etc. cannot be compared with assessee providing services in ITES segment - Held, yes [Para 21] [In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Res judicata/Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether where a company had outsourced considerable portion of its ITES business, it could not be compared to assessee carrying out entire operation by itself - Held, yes - Whether a company mainly engaged in providing high end services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise in field of data analytics and data process solutions was not comparable with assessee-company which was mainly engaged in providing low end services to group concerns - Held, yes - Whether a company having substantial goodwill being a parent company providing high end management solutions in health care was not comparable to assessee a captive service provider - Held, yes - Whether a consistent profit making company could not be rejected on ground that it had incurred loss in a particular year as functional comparability had to be seen - Held, yes - Whether where a company had been included/excluded from list of comparables in earlier years, consistent with view taken in earlier years and there being no change in facts and circumstances in instant year, same had to be included/excluded in list of final comparables - Held, yes [Paras 10 to 16][In favour of assessee]IT/ILT: Where a company had been included/excluded from list of comparables in earlier years, consistent with view taken in earlier years and there being no change in facts and circumstances in instant year, same had to be included/excluded in list of final comparables

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arms length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Assessee was engaged in providing ITeS to its AEs through use of information technology infrastructure including online software, live information services and research on international database - TPO benchmarked transactions of assessee using TNMM and selected nine comparables - It was noted that TPO took segmental information for income from engineering design services and treated it as IT enabled services - Whether since TPO failed to analyse how engineering design services of company could be compared with low end IT enabled services of assessee, comparable was to be rejected - Held, yes [Para 7][In favour of assessee]

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Segmental result) - Assessment year 2013-14 - Company was selected as a comparable by assessee itself in its TP Study - TPO accepted selected company as comparable to assessee - However, assessee later objected to its inclusion in list of comparables before TPO and DRP - Assessee's contentions in this regard were rejected by both TPO and DRP - In support of its contentions for exclusion of selected company from list of comparables, assessee submitted a copy of Annual Report of selected company for period under consideration and drew attention of Bench to various pages thereof as mentioned in chart filed in respect of comparable companies - Whether since before TPO and DRP, assessee has taken plea that selected company is engaged in products and technology innovation and that segmental information is not available but it was incumbent on TPO and DRP to have examined segmental details available in Annual Report of selected company and determine as to which of segments represents service segment and if such determination was possibie, then apply margin related to services segment only while carrying out comparability analysis with assessee - Held, Yes [Para 7.5.3] [In favour of assessee]

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2010-11 - During relevant year, assessee-company was rendering IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE - Whether a company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation took place, was not acceptable as valid comparable while determining ALP - Held, yes - Whether a company rendering technical services such as software testing, verification and validation of software item, implementation and data centre management activities, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company rendering ITES services after outsourcing same to third parties, could not be considered as comparable to assessee-company which was rendering exclusively in-house services - Held, yes [Paras 27.2 to 37] [Matter remanded]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Adjustments - Aggregation of transactions) - Assessment year 2011-12 - Assessee-company was engaged in provision of marketing support services to its AE outside India - It also rendered annual maintenance contract services to AEs as well as non-AEs, for products which were out of warranty period - TPO aggregated maintenance services to non AE with similar services rendered to AE as a single segment for comparability purpose under TNMM - Whether this was not permissible and since assessee had failed to furnish complete segmental information on actual basis before lower authorities, issue was remitted to file of TPO/Assessing Officer - Held, yes [Para 12] [Matter remanded]TRANSFER PRICING : Where TPO aggregated annual maintenance services to non-AE with similar services rendered to AE as a single segment for comparability purpose under TNMM, this was not possible and since complete segmental information on actual basis were not provided before lower authorities, issue was remitted to file of TPO/Assessing Officer  TRANSFER PRICING : Where details of employees cost had not been given by selected company and, therefore, it was not possible to ascertain, as to whether company passed employees cost filter applied by TPO, issue was to be remitted to TPO/Assessing Officer to consider relevant employees data and decide afresh  TRANSFER PRICING : Where there was substantial increase in revenue of selected company to tune of 30 per cent as compared to earlier years, which was usually abnormal, said company be excluded from comparables list  TRANSFER PRICING : Where entire revenue had been earned by selected company from sale of software services and products, since complete segmental details were not available, it could not be considered as comparable with software development services provider  TRANSFER PRICING : Where break-up of revenue from software services and software products was available in case of selected company, but break-up of operating costs and net operating revenues from these two segments had not been given, said company could not be treated as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING : Negative working capital adjustment shall not be made in case of a captive service provider as there is no risk and it is compensated on a total cost plus basis

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comprables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Assessee-company was engaged in rendering ITE services to its AE - Whether a company operating in different business strategy of acquiring companies for inorganic growth was incomparable to assessee - Held, yes - Company was less than 21.30 per cent and mostly it was with reference to outsourcing charges or translation charges, it could not be selected as a comparable company - Held, yes - Whether a company involved in diverse nature of services in absence of segmental data could not be selected as comparable - Held, yes - Whether where turnover of assessee was 63 crores, turnover of comparables should be in range of 1 crore to 200 crores - Held, yes [Paras 9 and 12] [In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations)- Assessment year 2010-11 - Whether in case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a company which had outsourced its significant work to outside ventures, was not acceptable as comparable - Held, yes [Para 23] [In favour of assessee]

VI. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Employees cost filter) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Assessee-company was engaged in rendering IT enabled services to its AE - Its employee cost was 62 per cent of total cost - On other hand, employee cost of comparable company was less than 2 per cent, which indicated that most of work was outsourced and outsourcing cost was at 88.64 per cent of operating cost - Whether, since, said company outsourced a considerable portion of its business, it was to be excluded from list of comparables to assessee - Held, yes [Para 26] [In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Assessee company a wholly owned subsidiary of a US company engaged into providing Information Technology (IT) Enabled Back Office support services relating to creation and maintenance of database of prospective employers -Whether a company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation had taken place during relevant year, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether where there was wide gap between employee cost of assessee vis-à-vis comparable company it could not be taken as valid comparable - Held, yes -Whether annual report is to be relied upon as against information under section 133(6), thus where there was contradiction in information supplied under section 133(6) stating activities of comparable to be in form of ITES whereas in annual report it was categorically mentioned that said comparable had only one segment i.e software development, it could not be taken as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a knowledge process outsourcing company engaged in providing consulting services, process outsourcing, process re-engineering and automation services, would not be a valid comparable for benchmarking international transaction qua ITES services undertaken by assessee - Held, yes - Whether companies having less than 25 per cent of sales as employee cost should not be chosen for comparability and hence had to be excluded - Held, yes - Whether a full-fledged risk taking company having diversifying business owning significant intangibles would not be comparable to assessee a minimal risk taking company having no intangibles- Held, yes - Whether company which had outsourced most of its services to other vendors/service providers would not be comparable to assessee being a captive provider engaged in back office work - Held, yes [Paras 17, 19, 22, 27, 32, 34, 37  40 ][Partly in favour of assessee]IT/ILT: A full-fledged risk taking company having diversifying business and owning significant intangibles would not be comparable to assessee a minimal risk taking company providing Information Technology (IT) Enabled Back Office support services and having no intangibles

facts.text:
The assessee-company was a wholly owned subsidiary of US company. It provided Research and Information Services and IT Support Services to its AE.

Operating Profit (OP)/Operating Cost (OC) was accepted as the Profit Level Indicator (PLI) by the TPO. However, out of 16 companies selected by the assessee as comparable companies, the TPO rejected 14 (including non-Indian companies). A final list of 8 comparable companies, including two companies chosen by the assessee was finally drawn up by the TPO proposing upward adjustment in respect of provision of IT Support Services and in respect of provision of Research and Information Services.

Disputes Resolution Panel (DRP) allowed part relief to the assessee.

By the impugned order. the Tribunal partly allowed the assessee's appeal and directed exclusion of four comparables, by applying stringent standards of comparability analysis to comparables selected under the Transaction Net Margin Method. Further, the Tribunal held concluding that nature of services provided by it under the R&I segment was in the nature of KPO services, whereas, according to assessee, it functioned more like a BPO.

On appeal:

The assessee-company was engaged in the business of software development services and ITES/BPO services. The assessee during the year under dispute provided such services only to its Associated Enterprise (AE). It had selected TNM Method as the most appropriate method and OP/TC as the profit level indicator for both the segments.

On reference, the TPO rejected the TP document of the assessee pointing out various defects and deficiencies. He undertook a search in the databases and computed the ALP of both the segments.

On the basis of transfer pricing adjustment computed by the TPO, the Assessing Officer passed the assessment order making certain additions.

The Commissioner (Appeals) dismissed the appeal of the assessee rejecting all its contentions.

The assessee objected to the following companies being treated as comparables in the software service segment:

(i)

Exensys Software Solutions Ltd.: The assessee submitted that not only the aforesaid company was involved in development of products but there was also an extraordinary event of merger during the relevant financial year.

(ii)

Thirdware Solutions Ltd.: The company was into development of product and involved in distribution activities. Therefore, it could not be treated as a comparable.

(iii)

Infosys Technologies Ltd.: The assessee contended that under no circumstances Infosys Technologies Ltd. could be treated as comparable to the assessee as it is a giant in the sector of software development and ITES having considerable brand value. The revenue, on the other hand, while strongly opposing contention of the assessee, submitted that the assessee itself in its own TP Study had selected Infosys Technologies Ltd. as a comparable.

The assessee had also sought exclusion of following comparable companies selected by the TPO in the ITES segment:

(i)

Vishal Information Technologies Ltd.: The company had outsourced a considerable part of its business to third party vendors. That was proved from the fact that only 2 per cent of the revenue was spent towards employee cost and there was huge vendor payment.

(ii)

Maple E Solutions Ltd.: The company could not be treated as comparable as the directors of the said company were found to be involved in fraud, hence financial results of the company could not be trusted as reliable.

(iii)

Wipro BPO Solutions Ltd.: WIPRO commands a premium in the pricing of its products and services due to goodwill, reputation and brand value. Therefore, it could not be compared to a risk mitigated captive service provider like the assessee.

The assessee, a BPO and a captive service provider, was providing ITE Services to its AEs.

The limited issue for adjudication in the present appeal was with reference to inclusion/exclusion of comparable companies. The assessee was seeking exclusion of, Domex, MPS, Vitae and Access Healthcare on the ground of functional disparity, extraordinary events and non-availability of segmental data.

The assessee was engaged in the software development and quality assurance-programme. It also acted as a call centre supporting inbound calls from its American AE. It selected 13 companies as comparable to its software development (IT) services segment and it selected 8 comparable companies to its ITES segment.

The TPO selected 11 comparable companies in the IT segment out of which 4 companies were common to the assessee and he selected 8 comparable companies in the ITES segment. In respect of both the segments a shortfall was determined as TP adjustment.

The DRP upheld the order of the TPO.

On appeal:

The assessee was engaged in providing voice-based customer care services to the clients of its AEs. It also rendered call centre services which fell within the broad description of Information Technology Enabled Services.

In consideration for the services, the AE remunerated the assessee by payment of all costs incurred by the assessee plus a mark up of fifteen per cent of the costs. The assessee chose eight comparable entities and the arithmetic average of the operating profit margins of the said comparables was computed at 15.74 per cent. According to the assessee, its PLI was within the acceptable range as indicated under the second proviso to section 92C and no T.P. adjustment was required.

The TPO identified a different set of comparable companies for the purpose of determining the ALP and computed the average operating profit margin of the comparable companies at 28.96 per cent on the basis of the average operating profit margin of eleven companies selected and computed the TP adjustment. On appeal, the DRP confirmed the said order.

The assessee appealed against the final assessment order on the ground that two comparables, namely, eClerx and Vishal could not be considered as comparable entities as the said companies were engaged in the business of Knowledge Process Outsourcing and, thus, could not be included as comparables.

The Tribunal rejected the assessee's contention and held that both eClerx and Vishal were engaged in providing ITeS and once a service fell within that category then no sub-classification of the segment was permissible. The Tribunal also held that KPO is a term given to the branch of BPO services where apart from processing of data, knowledge was also applied. The assessee's objection that the said two companies had abnormally high profits and thus ought to be excluded as comparables was also rejected.

■

The assessee-company was a captive contract software development service provider to its AEs and benchmarked the software development services segment under TNMM

■

The TPO, relying inter alia on information obtained under section 133(6), (i) included Ishir recording that Ishir met the employee cost filter (>25% of operating revenues) and the RPT filter, included Sasken Communication because it formed part of the assessee’s TP study and rejected the assessee’s exclusion based on an R&D-to-sales 3% filter, included Tata Elxsi and excluded Akshay Software on the basis that onsite revenue exceeded 75% of total revenue and, accordingly, made TP adjustment.

■

The DRP upheld the TPO’s order.

■

On the assessee’s appeal to the Tribunal : it is submitted that this is the second round of litigation for this appeal and the remand is qua the Software Development Segment (SWD segment) and given the scope of limited remand, other than the exclusion of Ishir , Sasken Communication , Tata Elxsi and inclusion of Akshay Software - no other comparable/issue can be argued.

The assessee-company was engaged in the business of ITeS in the field of architectural and interior designing. The assessee had entered into various international transactions with its Associated Enterprises (AEs).

The TPO rejected the assessee's submission and selected comparables in the ITeS segment and arrived at median (5th place) at 23.35 per cent. The Assessing Officer finally made a total adjustment on the international transaction relating to ITeS segment.

The assessee submitted that out of the comparables selected by the TPO, they want exclusion of only one comparable, i.e., Domex e-Data Pvt. Ltd. since the said company was functionally dissimilar as it was engaged in diversified services including software development, Knowledge Process Outsource (KPO), Business Process Outsource (BPO) and further that the segmental details were not available in the annual report.

The assessee was in the business of export of IT enabled back office service, in the field of insurance. It had adopted TNMM in its TP study. Considering itself to be in ITES segment doing low-end services, assessee had selected seven comparable companies which were the best comparables available. As per the assessee, average PLI of the comparables being 15.26 per cent, fell within the ± 5 per cent of its own PLI of 12.78 per cent.

The TPO rejected some of comparables. Thereafter the TPO made his own study and zeroed in on list of ten comparables including four from assessee's own list and, accordingly, made TP adjustment.

The DRP rejected some of the comparables.

On appeal:

The assessee, an Indian company was a wholly owned subsidiary of ISP Group having its headquarters in USA.

The business activity of the assessee was basically in two segments. The research and development services division which was engaged in providing research and development services to its group companies and the corporate support services division which was engaged in providing corporate support services (BPO services) to its group companies. The TPO accepted TNMM as the most appropriate method with OP/OC as the PLI for both the segments. He however, out of the seven comparables selected by assessee, retained five while rejecting the two companies and arithmetic mean of the five companies retained by TPO being 28.58 per cent as against OP/OC of 10 per cent shown by assessee, the ALP was determined and TP adjustment was made to BPO segment.

As regards, Research and development support services, the TPO selected two more companies and made TP adjustments accordingly.

The Assessing Officer made said adjustments.

DRP confirmed draft assessment order.

On appeal:

The assessee-company was engaged in providing IT and IT enabled services (ITeS) to Parexel Group companies which aid the clinical trial business.

The TPO proposed the TP adjustment.

In the ITES segment, DRP granted partial relief to the assessee by directing inclusion/exclusion of certain comparables.

On appeal, the assessee restricted its arguments towards inclusion/exclusion of certain comparables.

The assessee-company UHG India was into providing IT Enabled Health care services to UHG Group companies as a captive service provider. The assessee had two segments concerning international transactions viz. Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) and Software Development services. In its Transfer Pricing Study the assessee used TNMM as Most Appropriate Method (MAM) for both the segments and computed its margin at 13.83 per cent and 13.23 per cent in ITES and Software Development services respectively.

The TPO after examining the TP study made by the assessee and on the basis of various filters, made its own TP analysis by selecting 8 comparables for ITES segment and 18 comparables in software development segment and calculated their margin at 34.29 per cent and 28.88 per cent respectively and computed the cumulative adjustment in both the segments.

The DRP gave partial relief by excluding Bodhtree Consulting, CAT Technologies and Aricent Technologies from the final set of comparables qua software development services and by excluding Coral Hub qua ITES segment for benchmarking the international transaction.

On appeal to the Tribunal the assessee sought exclusion of 5 comparables and 3 comparables qua software development services and ITES segment respectively and also sought inclusion of 3 comparables qua ITES segment. The revenue also challenged exclusion of Bodhtree, CAT Technology qua software development segment and Coral Hub in ITES for benchmarking the international transaction.

The assessee-company rendered services mainly in two segments i.e., IT services and ITeS services. The IT services involved software development and maintenance of IT applications. The ITeS segment involved voice and non-voice-based services. The assessee entered into various international transactions with its Associate Enterprises (AE) under both segments.

Applying certain filters and after meeting assessee's objection with respect to exclusion/inclusion of comparable entities, TPO finalized three entities under IT segment and made TP adjustment accordingly.

Similar adjustment was made under ITeS Segment and 6 entities were selected having PLI of 18.38 per cent which led to another adjustment under this segment.

On appeal: the action of TPO was upheld.

On appeal:

The assessee was engaged in the business of providing data warehousing solutions in the nature of sales support and service of electronic data warehousing hardware and software. It entered into certain international transactions and benchmarked the same.

The TPO noted that for technical Support service such as hosting global consulting Centre, the assessee selected three comparables out of which one was rejected and, therefore, the margin of the comparables was determined at 29.41 per cent. With respect to infrastructure support services, the assessee computed the average margin of the comparables at 8.93 per cent, whereas TPO rejected the comparables of the assessee and further, introduced 26 comparables whose average margin was 28.45 per cent. He computed the margin of the assessee at 8.18 per cent. Thereafter, the TPO applied the weighted margin of all the three segments of the assessee based on segmental turnover to total turnover and determined weighted average of the margins of the comparable at 22.25 per cent. On that basis he computed the arm's length profit of the international transactions of the assessee against the actual profit and determined the adjustment because of transfer pricing. Further, with respect to the intra-group services of transaction value he computed ALP of the same at Rs. Nil.

The DRP directed the TPO to delete the adjustment with respect to intra-group services. Consequently, the DRP deleted the adjustments except on infrastructure support services where the only adjustment on the cost of infrastructure support services was required to be made. Based on this direction, the TPO recomputed the adjustment wherein the adjustment on account of ALP in infrastructure support services was made.

On appeal:

The assessee-company was engaged in providing routine software development (SD) and back office processing services (BPO), pursuant to a single composite contract to its AE for enabling it to service the same to end customers.

The assessee had entered into a single composite agreement/contract' with its AE to provide information technology based services (i.e., software development & support services (SD in short) and Back Office Process Outsourcing (BPO in short) services) on a 'bundled price basis'. Accordingly, the assessee had benchmarked the transaction pertaining to 'rendering of services' using Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) as the Most Appropriate Method (MAM) wherein the margin earned by the assessee from 'rendering of services' to AEs was determined to be at 27.50 per cent vis-a-vis 11.44 per cent earned by the comparable companies. Based on the said analysis, the transaction was determined to be at arm's length.

The TPO found from the audited accounts of the assessee company that it had three segments viz. BPO, Software Development and Support. He opined that the profitability from the software segment was at ALP. However, he observed that the profitability of BPO segment was quite low and the comparables for the same were to be determined.

The TPO proceeded to determine the ALP by searching on the Prowess Database the keyword 'ITES', i.e., searching for the comparables only in ITES segment. On the basis of mean margin earned by his own set of comparables, TPO made certain addition to the assessee's ALP.

The DRP agreed to the contention of the assessee it had rendered both SD and ITES services to its AE. The DRP directed the TPO to consider the comparables from IT or SD segment also for arriving at the ALP margin.

On cross appeals:

■

The assessee–company was engaged in manufacture, conversion and trading of diversified products and maintained six reportable segments, including a healthcare segment. It applied TNMM for its international transactions in the healthcare segment, earned a margin of 2.90% on sales, and selected five comparables with an arithmetic mean margin of 2.8%, claiming that its segmental results were at arm’s length. The assessee had made payments to its associated enterprise towards administration and business support/IT support services relating to its IT infrastructure. In AY 2008-09, it reported payment of about Rs. 6.12 crores under this head.

■

The TPO rejected the assessee’s study, conducted a fresh search on Prowess and Capitaline, and selected six comparables with an arithmetic mean margin of 14.55% on sales. He retained six comparables and determined margins at 17.10% on OP/OC and 12.22% on OP/Sales for the healthcare segment. He computed arm’s length operating revenue at about Rs. 76.16 crores against actual operating cost of about Rs. 84.25 crores, and proposed a transfer pricing adjustment of about Rs. 8.09 crores under section 92CA. He did not exclude manufacturing companies since, in his view, the assessee also had manufacturing activity and had itself considered a manufacturer (Hicks Thermometer (I) Ltd.) in comparability. The TPO treated the services as intra-group services for which, according to him, the assessee failed to demonstrate rendition and benefit, and applying CUP determined the arm’s length price at Nil, proposing a transfer pricing adjustment of about Rs. 6.12 crores under section 92CA for AY 2008-09.

■

On appeal, the CIT(A) partly allowed the assessee’s appeal. Recording that, as per the assessee’s TP study, trading constituted about 93.1% of sales and conversion/manufacturing about 6.7%, the CIT(A) characterized the assessee’s healthcare segment as predominantly trading. The CIT(A) held Poly Medicure Ltd. to be an exclusively manufacturing-based company (with trading revenue of about 1.39% from inputs) and Opto Circuits (India) Ltd. to have about 91% revenue from manufacturing, and directed exclusion of both from the comparables for the healthcare segment. For AY 2009-10, the CIT(A) directed similar exclusion of Poly Medicure Ltd. and Opto Circuits (India) Ltd. from the comparables on identical grounds. The CIT(A) deleted the adjustment attributable to IT support services, holding that the assessee had paid only maintenance charges for its IT infrastructure (servers, application software and network services, including help desk and disaster recovery/business continuity back-up). The CIT(A) noted that substantial project implementation expenditure of about Rs. 3.89 crores incurred in FY 2004-05 for the IT set-up had already been accepted in AY 2005-06 and, following consistency, accepted the maintenance-related expenditure for the year. For AY 2009-10, the CIT(A) directed acceptance of payment towards IT support services of about Rs. 61.34 lakhs.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal.

Assessee was engaged in providing software development and call centre services only to its AE. Being the captive service provider, it was remunerated for the services on the basis of cost +15 per cent mark-up. During the year, assessee had provided software development services and call centre services.

In TP study, in the software development services segment, assessee selected a set of 17 comparable companies with an average of 10.86 per cent and justified its arm's length price (ALP) of 15.35 per cent. In the call centre service agreement, assessee selected set of 22 comparable companies with the margin of 13.30 per cent viz-a-viz that of 15.46 per cent of assessee.

However, the TPO did not accept assessee's TP study and proposed to reject 13 out of 17 comparable companies in the software development services and selected new companies. In the call centre service segment also, the TPO accepted six comparables and proposed 25 new comparables and accordingly proposed certain TP adjustment.

The DRP rejected the assessee's contentions.

On appeal, the assessee objected to comparables selected by the TPO in both segments and rejection of assessee's TP study.

The assessee-company was providing infrastructure support IT services as a help desk to cater to the foreign clients of CompuCom, USA.

The assessee objected to the inclusion of a company by stating that it was engaged in dissimilar business, dissimilar employee cost and exceptional high margins. The TPO rejected the assessee's contention of high profit margin by holding that once arithmetic mean of profit margins of the comparables was taken, there remained no net to exclude companies with super profit margins. The TPO, however, did not discuss the other dissimilarities pointed out by the assessee.

The DRP observed that the TPO selected only the 'Prepress-BPO' segment of this company, which was comparable to the ITES activities of the assessee. No relief was, therefore, allowed by the DRP on this count.

■

The assessee, a captive service provider and wholly owned subsidiary of a US company, was engaged in providing technical support and payroll administrative services to its AEs. The TPO determined an arm’s length price adjustment of about ₹3.97 crore, which was incorporated by the Assessing Officer in the draft assessment order; the DRP upheld the TPO’s approach and granted working capital adjustment on comparables.

■

In the first round (June 2018), the Tribunal remitted, inter alia, (i) the issue of inclusion/exclusion of HSCC to the TPO to verify from annual accounts and other details whether HSCC had received any grant/incentive and whether it was engaged in diversified activities, with a direction to consider the Tribunal’s order for assessment year 2011–12 where HSCC was excluded; and (ii) the comparability of Mitcon to the TPO to examine whether related party transactions exceeded the prescribed threshold and whether segmental data was available, and to decide the issue in light of the Tribunal’s order for assessment year 2011–12 where Mitcon was rejected.

■

Pursuant to the remand, the TPO (January 2021) held that HSCC had not received any government grant or incentive and was functionally similar to the assessee, and accordingly included it as a comparable. Similarly, the TPO held that Mitcon satisfied the RPT filter and that segmental data was available in the public domain, and, based on its annual report and website, treated it as functionally comparable. Consequently, the TP adjustment was reduced to about ₹1.78 crore, which was incorporated by the Assessing Officer in the final assessment order.

■

On appeal, the Commissioner(Appeals) upheld the inclusion of HSCC, observing that the TPO had verified its annual accounts and found no receipt of grants/incentives, and treated it as a functionally similar company passing all filters. The Commissioner(Appeals) also sustained inclusion of Mitcon, holding that the TPO had complied with the Tribunal’s directions regarding RPT filter and segmental data.

■

On appeal before the Tribunal.

The assessee was engaged in providing software development solutions (SWD) and IT consultancy services (ITES) to its group companies. It was also providing back-office support services through its AEs.

It applied certain filters and selected certain comparables for benchmarking its both the SWD and ITES segments.

The TPO rejected the assessee's TP study report and selected fresh set of companies for both the SWD and ITES segments of the assessee. Further, the TPO observed that the assessee had not made any adjustment on outstanding receivables, therefore, he calculated using LIBOR 6 months plus 450 basis points on outstanding receivables. Accordingly, he made TP adjustment towards international transactions.

The DRP gave partial relief to the assessee.

On the assessee's appeal to the Tribunal:

The assessee provided software development services as well as ITES to its AE.

After examination of the TP study of the assessee and considering the objections of the assessee, the TPO arrived at the final set of comparables and made TP adjustment.

Pursuant to the directions of the DRP, while there was no variation in the ITeS segment, the TPO revised the margin computation of the comparable companies in the IT Services.

The assessee, a subsidiary Mauritius based company, was engaged in providing IT enabled services. It had selected TNMM as MAM and had computed margin at 15.06 on operating cost.

The TPO had conducted fresh analysis and applied certain filters and selected fresh set of comparables. Accordingly, he determined the adjustment in the ITES segment.

The DRP upheld the order of the TPO.

On the assessee's appeal to the Tribunal:
