[Para 12.2] The material on record suggests that outsourcing charges of comparable constitute 90 per cent of the total operating cost in this case. On a specific query, the revenue admitted that our assessee is engaged in the business of doing activities at its own without any outsourcing. This crucial factor, having a greater bearing on the profitability, makes it distinguishable from the assessee. The Mumbai Bench of the Tribunal in the case of Asstt. CIT v. Hapag Lloyd Global Services (P.) Ltd. [IT Appeal No. 8499 (Mum.) of 2010, dated 28-2-2013] has held that Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. cannot be considered as comparable because of the overwhelming outsourcing activity carried out by it. This view was taken by relying on another order passed by the Mumbai Bench of the Tribunal in Asstt. CIT v. Maersk Global Service Center (India) (P.) Ltd. [2011] 133 ITD 543/16 taxmann.com 47. In the later case also, the Tribunal held that the case of Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. or Coral Hub Ltd. was not includible in the list of comparables because of major outsourcing. Since the facts of the instant case are on all fours with these two cases, it is opined that this case is required to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 12.3]

Cosmic Global Limited

From the material on record it is apparent that outsourcing charges of this case constitute 57.31 per cent of the total operating costs. This does not appear to be a valid reason for eliminating this case from the list of comparables. On going through the Annual accounts of Cosmic Global Limited, it is found that its total revenue from operations are at Rs.7.37 crore divided into three segments, namely, Medical transcription and consultancy services at Rs.9.90 lakhs, Translation charges at Rs.6.99 crore and Accounts BPO at Rs.27.76 lakhs. The assessee has made out a case that outsourcing activity carried out by this company constitutes 57 per cent of total expenses.

When one is examining the results of this company from the Accounts BPO segment alone, there is no need to examine the position under other segments. The entire outsourcing is confined to Translation charges paid at Rs.3.00 crore, which is strictly in the realm of the Translation segment, revenues from which are to the tune of Rs.6.99 crore. If this segment of Translation is not under consideration for deciding as to whether this case is comparable or not, one cannot take recourse to the figures which are relevant for segments other than accounts BPO. Thus it is held that this case cannot be excluded on the strength of outsourcing activity, which is alien to the relevant segment. [Para 13.2]

However, this case is found to incomparable on the alternative argument advanced by the assessee to the effect that total revenue of the Accounts BPO segment of Cosmic Global Limited is very low at Rs.27.76 lakhs. A captive unit cannot be compared with a giant case. As the segmental revenue of BPO segment of Cosmic Global Limited at Rs. 27.76 lakh is still on much lower side, this case is, therefore, directed to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 13.3]

Genesys International Corporation Ltd.

The assessee is basically providing various services to the customers of its AEs in relation to human resources which are more or less centered around the employees of the prospective clients. When one consider the nature of services provided by Genesys International Corporation Ltd., it comes to the forefront that they are providing full range of geospatial services to its customers. In simple terms, geospatial services means the services relating to the relative position of things on the earth's surface. These basically include 3D mapping, Navigation maps, Image processing, Cadastral mapping, etc. If one takes into account the nature of services provided by the assessee, being financial and retirement security, health, productivity of employees and employment relationships and then try to compare them with those rendered by Genesys, it is manifested that both are totally incomparable. The High Court further held that where the controlled transactions are clearly in the nature of low-end ITES as in the case of assessee being a captive provider engaged in back office work, for rendering data processing not involving domain knowledge, inclusion of KPO service provider as comparable would not be warranted and the transfer pricing study would be impacted at the threshold. The High Court ordered to exclude VISHAL as a comparable for ALP determination of Rampgreen Solutions (P.) Ltd. (supra) engaged in ITES business by observing that Vishal could not be considered as a comparable, as admittedly, its business model was completely different. Admittedly, Vishal's expenditure on employment cost during the relevant period was a small fraction of the proportionate cost incurred by the assessee, apparently, for 'the reason that most of its work was outsourced to other vendors/service providers. Plainly, a business model where services are rendered by employing own employees and using one's own infrastructure would have a' different cost structure as compared to a business model where services are outsourced. There was no material for the Tribunal to conclude that the outsourcing of services by Vishal would have no bearing on the profitability of the said entity. [Para 37]

On cross appeals:

HELD: Comparable Vishal Information Technologies Ltd.

This company is, inter alia, engaged in e-publishing, which is an activity similar to the one done by the assessee. Even the activities of 'data digitisation' and 'print on demand conversion' are also similar to those undertaken by the assessee. However, despite having functionally similarity to a greater extent, this company cannot be considered as comparable because of a different business model adopted by it. Its annual accounts for the year ending 31-3-2007 are available on record. It can be seen that 'Operating expenses' are to the tune of Rs. 17.35 crores out of which a sum of Rs. 13.12 crores is on account of 'Data entry charges & Vendor Payments'. This shows that 75 per cent of the operating expenses of this company are on outsourcing. As against this, the assessee's job work to total cost ratio is only 5 per cent. This demonstrates that Vishal Information Technologies Ltd., though in almost similar line of business functionally, ceases to be comparable, because of the adoption of a different business model as per which the activities are mostly outsourced. In contrast, the assessee is providing majority of its activities in-house. It goes without saying that there is a marked difference in profitability when the services are outsourced or provided in-house. Similar view has been taken by the Tribunal in several cases removing Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. on the basis of such business model. Under such circumstances, the Tribunal consider Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. as not comparable and directed to eliminate it from the list of comparables. The view taken by the Commissioner (Appeals) in continuing to include this company in the final set of comparables is, therefore, overturned. [Para 6.2]

As the facts of the year under consideration are similar, the decision rendered in the earlier year would apply to the year under consideration as well. In this factual view of the matter, it is to be held that Infosys BPO, stands on a totally different footing from a company engaged in rendering routine back office ITES; being both functionally different and having brand value and, therefore, is to be excluded from the final set of comparables. It is also to be observed that the TPO himself has reached the same conclusion in the subsequent assessment year 2015-16; that the Infrastructure segment services segment is not comparable to ITES. The annual report of 'Microland' for the year under consideration, the segmental details of the two business segments are provided from which it is seen that out of the total revenue of Rs. 34.471 lakhs, the revenue from ITES segment is Rs. 1959 lakhs; which is 5.68 per cent of the total revenue. As, it is already been concluded that the infrastructure services segment is a different business segment not comparable to ITES rendered; this company, 'Microland' fails the filter adopted by the TPO that companies whose service income is less than 75 per cent of total operating revenue are to be excluded. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, as discussed above, and in view of the above factual findings, company Microland is to be excluded from the final set of comparables in the case on hand. [Para 8.4.4]

Comparable Company Informed Technologies:

This company 'Informed' is engaged in and operating as an ITES provider. A perusal of the TPO's order also indicates that the TPO has not disputed that this company is functionally comparable to the assessee in the case on hand; which is rendering back office ITES. From a perusal of the profit and loss account of 'Informed' it is seen that the total revenue is shown as Rs. 3.81 crores and 'other income' of Rs. 1.22 crores. From the Annual Report of this company, it is to be seen that the 'other income' comprises of non-operating income, interest, dividend, sale of current investments and miscellaneous income and evidently these incomes cannot be considered as operating income. The percentage of 67.7 per cent worked out by the TPO is after considering these 'other income' as service income; which is factually incorrect. It is evident from a perusal of the profit and loss account of 'Informed' that the service income is Rs. 2.58 crores which is entirely the revenue from operations and, therefore, the service income filter of 75 per cent of service income to be from ITES as applied by the TPO, is satisfied in this case. In view of this factual finding rendered in the matter, this company 'Informed Technologies' satisfies the service income filter and, therefore,is to be included in the final set of comparables. [Para 10.4.1]

Comparable Crystal Voxx:

data of Coral Hub Limited for the then current year alone. The assessee thereafter requested the TPO to exclude the case from the list of comparables. The TPO refused to do so. The Tribunal, however, rightly excluded the Coral Hub Limited from the list of comparables. [Para 34]

The revenue firstly contended that once an assessee seeks the inclusion of a case in the list of comparables, it cannot subsequently insist the same on being excluded. [Para 35] There is nothing to support this view either in law or in principle. The aim is to determine the ALP. The exercise requires the assessment of the relevant data. If the data furnished is not relevant or comparable it cannot possibly be considered merely because the assessee has relied upon it. If the TPO finds the data to be irrelevant he is not only entitled but bound to exclude it from consideration. There is no reason then why the TPO cannot do so on the application of the assessee. Indeed if the case is comparable, the TPO is not bound to reject it merely because the assessee applies to have it excluded. Whether or not to exclude the case from the list of comparables depends upon the relevance of the case and not the desire of the parties. [Para 36]

The next question is whether Coral Hub Limited ought to be included in the list of comparables. The ground on which the assessee contends that Coral Hub Limited ought to be excluded from the list of comparables is also well founded. Coral Hub Limited outsources a significant portion of its work. The finding is that the outsourcing charges constitute 90 per cent of the total operating costs. It is admitted by the department that the assessee on the other hand conducts its activities itself without outsourcing any part of it. There can be no comparison between an enterprise that conducts its business activities itself with one that outsources its activities although the activities pertain to the same field. The entire administrative set up of such enterprises would be different. An entity that outsources most of its work is not required to maintain a large establishment. For instance, it would be necessary for such an enterprise to have large premises and a large number of employees. Even the material it uses and the equipment that it installs from minor items such as stationery and telephones to electrical fittings and even machinery are bound to be far less than the material and equipment that an enterprise which conducts its activities itself would of necessity be required to maintain. [Para 37]

This in turn would also have consequences upon the legal requirements to be fulfilled by the two enterprises. There are several enactments that bring within its ambit, establishments or undertakings that employ a certain number of persons. There are enactments that also bring within their ambit enterprises that use power. This in turn would require an enterprise carrying on its own activities to maintain staff along with attendant facilities to ensure compliance with such legislation. The financial difference between such enterprises is bound to be enormous. [Para 38]

The Tribunal's decision not to consider this case is, therefore, correct. [Para 40]

In the result, revenue's appeal is dismissed.

HELD: Universal Print Systems Ltd. (Segment BPO)

On similar facts (i.e., company fails the employees cost filter and is functionally different), as in the case on hand a co-ordinate Bench of this Tribunal in the case of CGI Information Systems & Management Consultants (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2018] 94 taxmann.com 97 (Bang. - Trib.), also for assessment year 2012-13, has remanded the issue of comparability analysis at the segmental level to the file of the TPO for examination and verification wherein it was held that there appears to be no bar in the rule 10B to consider segmental data under TNMM because the comparison is of 'net profit margin realized by the enterprise from an international transaction' with the 'net profit realized from a comparable uncontrolled transaction'. Therefore comparison is of similar transaction. When segmental information is available and is not disputed, it cannot be argued that filters have to be applied at entity level. It cannot be argued that when the TPO himself applied the filters at the entity level he was not entitled to apply the filters at segmental level. If clear segmental information is available the filters can be applied at the segmental level in TNMM. Therefore, the objection with regard to this company failing the employee cost filter and service revenue filter was rightly rejected by the TPO and DRP. It is however seen that this company has four segments viz., Repro, Label Printing, Offset Printing and Pre-press BPO. Whether the label printing and offset printing segments supplement the functions performed in the Pre-press BPO segment has to be seen. We therefore set aside the order of the DRP in this regard and remand for fresh consideration by the TPO the comparability of this company. In terms of rule 10B(3) of the Rules the profit margins of Pre-Press BPO have to be adjusted taking into account the fact that two other segments supplement the pre-press BPO segment. If such adjustment cannot be reasonably or accurately made then this company has to be excluded from the list of comparable companies. The TPO for this purpose can use his powers under section 133(6) to get required details from this company. As far as the argument that this company fails functional comparability, that none of the objections raised by the assessee in this regard about lack of information about allied services performed by the pre-press BPO segment of this company and the break-up of the revenue from such allied services have been dealt with specifically by the TPO or DRP. Since the comparability of this company is being remanded to be TPO for consideration of adjustments as mentioned above, the objection with regarded to functional comparability should also be looked into by the TPO in the remand proceedings on the basis of materials which he may gather under section 133(6). The assessee should be given opportunity of being heard by the TPO before the issue is decided by the TPO.

Moreover, since the RPT was only 28.08 per cent which was marginally above 25 per cent, it does not have significant effect on the profitability keeping in view the filters applied by TPO. Therefore, the assessee's contention on this count was rejected. As far as the assessee's second plea regarding outsourcing of substantial amount of work is concerned, in the objections filed before DRP it is stated that outsourced cost to total expenses was 22.07 per cent. Thus, the VITL could not be considered as comparable company and was to be excluded from the list of comparable companies. The assessee-company itself agreed before the TPO that VITL was a comparable company offering IT enabled services and this company was an extension of one Indian company, having agreed so it was not correct on the part of the assessee-company to raise a new plea that the VITL had to pay low wages as compared to the assessee-company. It appeared that the VITL had outsourced the manpower and the cost of outsourcing appeared to have been included in the other heads of the expenditure instead of wages-employee cost. Moreover, the intangibles would not materially affect the price or profit earning. By outsourcing the manpower, the VITL would have incurred more cost compared to the assessee-company, thus resulting in lesser operating profit. But, having considering the findings of the TPO, it was found that the intangibles or outsourcing the manpower would not materially affect the price or profit margin. No two comparable companies can be replicas of each other. The application of rule 10B should be carried out and judged not with technical rigor, but on a broader prospective. In this view of the matter, there was no infirmity in the order of the Commissioner (Appeals) in confirming the action of the TPO by selecting the VITL as comparable company. [Para 36]

Another issue was as to whether the TPO was correct in selecting 'W' BPO having turnover of 20 times more than the assessee-company as comparable or not. It was found that this issue was covered in favour of the assessee by the decision of Delhi ITAT in the case of Agnity India Technologies (P.) Ltd [IT Appeal No. 3856/Delhi/2010]. The 'W' BPO was not at all comparable as the assessee-company was pigmy compared to giant 'W'. Turnover of 'W' BPO was 20 times more than the assessee-company. Hence, the assessee-company was not comparable with 'W' BPO, the reasoning being that the latter was a giant company having 20 times more turnover than the assessee-company. In view of this, based on the facts and the circumstances of the case, and following the decision of Delhi Bench of ITAT in the aforesaid case, it was opined that 'W' BPO should be excluded from the list of comparable companies. [Para 37]

The next issue was with regard to the rejection of ASL as comparable company in back office services segment on the basis that the company sourced its business exclusively from Apex Data Services Inc., USA and thus, had related party transactions. It was found that ASL did not render any services to Apex Data but only sourced business from them. Therefore, ASL rendered services directly to the third parties and not to the Apex Data. The assessee clearly demonstrated that ASL had only transaction with Apex Data in purchasing of fixed assets. Relevant papers were placed on record by the assessee. In view of this matter, it was found that there was no controlled transaction between the ASL and Apex Data. Thus, no materially significant related party transactions existed section 92A(2)(i) clearly deals with manufacturing of goods and articles and not with provision of services. Therefore, the TPO/Commissioner (Appeals) was not justified in rejecting the ASL as comparable company from the final list of comparable companies. [Para 38]

The view point of the authorities in forcefully including a company in the list of comparables simply on the ground that since the assessee initially voluntarily treated it as comparable, now it cannot resile, cannot be appreciated. The substance of the matter is to consider and decide the comparability of a company with the assessee on merits rather than harping on an inadvertent mistake committed by the assessee in this regard. If an assessee wrongly includes a company in the list of comparables and then puts up a case before the TPO that this company is, in fact, not comparable citing the reasons for its stand, the TPO is obliged to reject the contention under due process of law after successfully meeting with the objections so raised by the assessee. It cannot be a one sided wind blow. There can be no estoppel against the inclusion of correct companies in the tally of comparables. If one has to go strictly with the assessee's list of comparables by not accepting the contention for the exclusion of a particular company after proper evaluation, then, there ought to be complete acceptance of the assessee's version as regards the comparability of all other companies as well. There cannot be simultaneous approbate and reprobate. As the position is not so and TPO is fully empowered to examine and evaluate each and every company included by the assessee in its list of comparables from the angle of its actual comparability, in the like manner, the TPO should also examine the assessee's contention of incomparability of a company wrongly included by it in the list of comparables, if argued. [Para 13]

Regarding rejection of the comparables given by the assessee in its TP report on the ground that some of the companies were loss making companies, the assessee had explained as to how in some cases there was actually profit and as to how despite losses those were comparable transactions. This aspect had however not been considered by the Assessing Officer at all. In the set aside proceedings before the Assessing Officer, the Assessing Officer would consider this aspect also.[Para 31] It was the submission of the assessee that ITES-BPO sector consisted of various segments and each segment was functionally different from the other. It was the claim of the assessee that it fell under the category of customer care which was at the lowest strata of ITES-BPO sector. The assessee was a call centre answering various customer queries. The assessee for carrying out its work had to employ candidates who were graduates/undergraduates with english speaking skills and need not hold any specific skill like accountants, legal professionals, software professionals, executives, technical consultants, creative agents. The ITES-BPO sector provides higher end services like payment services, HR, Payroll, Finance and Accounts which require personnel with specific skills sets like Accountant, HR Professionals having post degree qualification in HR, etc. It had been the claim of the assessee that as one goes higher in the ITES-BPO sector ladder, the job is more complex and therefore billing rate per hour and resultant margin charged for services was bound to be higher. Thus, the assessee claimed that the BPO sector selected by the TPO (9 companies) were not mere call centre but performing much more skilled jobs than that of a call centre. The TPO had ignored the plea of the assessee and had not given any reasons for doing so. The TPO had merely said that the comparable instances were performing identical job as performed by the assessee. Such rejection of the assessee without assigning any reason was arbitrary. [Para 32]

Another aspect which was noticed from the TPO's order was that he had carried out FAR analysis and had alleged that the assessee was performing services that were much more technical than what an ordinary call centre performed. The TPO had not spelt out as to how in the comparative uncontrolled transaction considered by the TPO, the nature of services rendered was similar to the one rendered by the assessee.[Para 33]

One of the submission made by the assessee was that, if for any reason, the Tribunal remanded the issue of determination of arm's length price (ALP) to the Assessing Officer, then, a direction would be given that the TPO would not look afresh into data that was available in the public domain. According to him the Transfer Pricing (TP) study was required to be done on the basis of data available in the public domain at the point of time when the TP study was undertaken by the assessee and any new data available should not be considered, since the assessee could not foresee data which was not available in public domain when it determined ALP. According to him, if the TPO was permitted to do so, then it would be an endless exercise, which would put the assessee in a disadvantageous position. [Para 34]

So long as the data available before the TPO in the course of proceedings pursuant to the order of the Tribunal is contemporaneous in point of time and is otherwise comparable, there was no reason as to why the TPO should be precluded from looking into such data. After all the exercise of determining the ALP involves approximation and is to some extent notional. The idea is to fix the ALP. Any uncontrolled comparable transaction which is available in public domain cannot therefore be ignored. The assessee would not be prejudiced in any manner, if such data was looked into by the TPO. The assessee can always have objections to such data being used. However, it was to be emphasized that the data so used should be contemporaneous in point of time and should be comparable. Even rule 10B(4) of the Rules contemplated this and it lays down that the data to be used in analyzing the comparability of an uncontrolled transaction with an international transaction shall be the data relating to the financial year in which the international transaction has been entered into. Thus, there are adequate safeguards in the rules and the assessee's apprehension was not well founded.[Para 35]

The Tribunal in Maersk Global Centres India (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2014] 147 ITD 83/43 taxmann.com 100 (Mum. - Trib) while specifically dealing with the comparability of the aforesaid company to a ITES provider, has held that since the company engaged in providing engineering design service which was a high end service in the nature of KPO, it cannot be treated as comparable. Comparable eClerx Services Ltd.

As per the annual report of this company, it is noted that the company is engaged in offering solutions in the field of data analytics, operations management, audits and re-conciliation, matrics management and reporting services. In fact, the Delhi High Court in Rampgreen Solutions (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2015] 377 ITR 533/234 Taxman 573/60 taxmann.com 355, has held that this company being a KPO service provider cannot be considered as a comparable to ITES companies. Therefore, respectfully following said view, eClerx Services Ltd. being functionally different, cannot be treated as comparable to the assessee.

Comparable Vishal Technologies Ltd.

No doubt, assessee in the transfer pricing study has selected this company as a comparable. It is also a fact either before the Transfer Pricing Officer or the DRP, assessee has not raised any specific objection in respect of the aforesaid company. Even then, assessee's objection cannot be overruled for that reason alone. When the Transfer Pricing Officer has rejected the transfer pricing analysis of the assessee the department cannot use it selectively to their advantage. The assessee has sought exclusion of this comparable company mainly on the ground that it outsources most of its work which is 57.31 per cent as compared to the assessee which is only 2.5 per cent and employee cost of this company is lower. Though this is fairly a vital factor vitiating the comparability, however, the assessee could not give any rebuttal or any cogent reasons as to why this comparable company was selected and chosen by the assessee after carrying out FAR analysis not only in earlier years, but also in subsequent assessment years i.e. 2010-11 and 2011-12 again on carrying same FAR analysis. It is only in this year that assessee is seeking exclusion on the ground that it has a different business model. Such pick and choose of comparables every year according to the suitability of the margin definitely amounts to cherry picking. The assessee has not demonstrated that in earlier years and subsequent years the business model of Cosmic Global Ltd. is different, i.e., it does not outsource its substantial work. No doubt assessee can object to inclusion or exclusion of a comparable company contrary to its TP Study Report by citing cogent grounds and pointing out the factors vitiating the comparability and TPO has to examine these comparability factors on merits, but when assessee consistently adopts any comparable company and too after FAR scrutiny then onus is very heavy upon the assessee to substantiate that the material factors in the relevant year are different from the years when it seeks to take contrary stand in a particular year. The assessee has been unable to point out the material factors for distinction sought in this year was not permeating in the earlier years or in the subsequent years. This inconsistent approach cannot be permitted as it can lead to falling in the realm of whims of suitability of assessee. Had it been the case where material facts were different in this year and the comparable has been selected on some incorrect analysis in the earlier year or at the time of TP study, then definitely there cannot be any estoppel for objecting to for exclusion, but such material facts and incorrect approach has to be demonstrated which has not been done in this year. This inconsistency is further accentuated by the fact that this comparable continues to be part of assessee's comparable in subsequent years. In relation to the financial year under consideration, the business model in which Cosmic Global Ltd. has functioned is quite dissimilar to the business model of the assessee while carrying out the activity of an ITES provider. Moreover, none of the objections raised by the assessee have been met by the TPO on the basis of any cogent reasoning. On that count also, the plea of the assessee to exclude Cosmic Global Ltd. from the final set of comparables is justified. The objection of the TPO that the said concern was found comparable by the assessee in earlier year cannot be the sole basis to include the said concern in the list of comparables, [Para 19]

Comparable Eclerx Services Ltd.

The Tribunal in Capital IQ Information Systems (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Addl. CIT [2014] 49 taxmann.com 313 (Hyd.) has held that as seen from the Annual Report, the above company is involved in diverse nature of services and there was no segmental data for diversified service portfolio. Moreover this company should be considered as KPO and this company is not comparable to assessee's services. [Para 22]

Thus, the plea of the assessee that the said concern is functionally dissimilar to the assessee, has been wrongly rejected by the TPO. Even there is no cogent reasoning brought out by the revenue to assail assessee's plea for exclusion of Eclerx Services Ltd. from the final set of comparables. [Para 23]

Comparable Coral Hubs Ltd.

engaged in business of providing IT enabled services to its AEs - TPO did not agree with various filters used by assessee in its TP study and selected certain new comparables - TPO while calculating PLI of comparables had taken miscellaneous income as operating in nature -Assessee submitted that miscellaneous income should be non-operating in absence of details and nature of miscellaneous income received by comparables - However, TPO/Assessing Officer had not made any effort to look into this aspect - Whether therefore, matter was to be remanded back to TPO/Assessing Officer for adjudication afresh - Held, yes [Para 24] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT : Matter remanded to TPO/Assessing Officer to decide whether in absence of details and nature of miscellaneous income received by comparables, miscellaneous income could have been taken to be operating in nature  IT/ILT : Where TPO while calculating PLI of comparables had himself accepted that donation and provision for doubtful debt was non-operating, same was to be applied while calculating PLI of assessee also  IT/ILT : Matter remanded to TPO/Assessing Officer to verify evidences/bills/details/correspondence relating to expenditure incurred on non-operational unit of assessee and to decide whether they were operating/non-operating expenses  IT/ILT : Company engaged in digital library and print on demand in case of which segmental details were not available would not be comparable to company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs  IT/ILT : Company engaged in rendering software development and engineering design services would not be comparable to company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs  IT/ILT : A giant company having huge asset base, brand value, goodwill and presence in global market and being a full fledged risk bearing service provider having significant R  D activities would not be comparable to IT enabled service provider  IT/ILT : Company engaged in healthcare receivables cycle management in which case extraordinary events of amalgamation and acquisition had taken place during relevant year, however, no segmental details were available, would not be comparable to company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs  IT/ILT : A company engaged in data analytics and financial services, in which extraordinary event of acquisition had taken place during year, would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : A company in which an extraordinary event of acquisition of a group during relevant year had taken place would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : Company engaged in providing geographical information services comprising photogrammetric, remote sensing cartonography, data conversion, related computer based services and other related services being functionally different would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : Where ITES segment of a company was similar to that of assessee-company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs, but there was discrepancy in annual report and in information gathered under section 133(6), said company could not have been taken as comparable  IT/ILT : Company engaged in product development and for which no segmental data was available, would not be comparable to company providing IT enabled services to its AE  IT/ILT : Where ITES activities of a company included data centre management services, end user computing services, managed security services, which were not functionally similar to that of assessee company providing IT enabled services to its AE, said company had to be excluded from final list of comparables

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company providing high-level services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise and being a leading provider of KPO services would not be functionally comparable to assessee engaged in providing low-end ITES enabled call centre services to its AE - Held, yes - Whether assessee-company having a business model where services were rendered by employing own employees and using one's own infrastructure would have a different cost structure as compared to a business model where services were outsourced and hence would not be comparable - Held, yes - Whether where DRP had omitted to record any finding regarding comparability of a company, matter required readjudication - Held, yes - Whether assessee would be permitted to raise objections against a comparable first time before Tribunal, but adjudication on inclusion/exclusion of this company from final list of comparables was to be restored to file of TPO - Held, yes [Para 16] [In favour of assessee/Matter remanded]IT/ILT: Company providing high-level services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise and being a leading provider of KPO services would not be functionally comparable to assessee, a BPO engaged in providing low-end ITES enabled call centre services to its AE

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparable, factor to determine - Segmental results) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company had earned revenue from information technology/BPO related services and sales from infra activities, but due to non-availability of reliable segmental data, said company could not be considered to be comparable to assessee rendering ITE services - Held, yes [Para 20] [In favour of assessee]  II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITeS)) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company was KPO company and earned revenue from data analytics services and process solutions, it could not be compared with assessee rendering ITE services - Held, yes [Para 24] [In favour of assessee]  III. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (comparability factors - Segmental result) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company operated in 3 segments and had un-allocable expenses which rendered its financial information relating to aforesaid 3 segments unreliable, said company could not be considered to be comparable - Held, yes [Para 27] [In favour of assessee]  IV. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Others) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where TPO rejected a company as a comparable on basis that it had negative net worth but it was found that TPO had computed net worth of company incorrectly and for year under consideration, correct net worth of company was not negative, said company could be compared with assessee rendering ITeS - Held, yes [Para 30] [In favour of assessee]  V. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Export filter) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where entire revenue of selected company was from domestic contracts, whereas assessee's entire earnings was from export of business support services, said company could not be considered to be functionally comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Para 33] [In favour of assessee]  VI. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Data in public domain) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Whether where selected company was proposed to be considered as a comparable by TPO but data pertaining to this company was not provided to assessee by TPO, in absence of data being available in public domain, selected company could not be considered as comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Para 36] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - ITES) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether company deriving significant portion of its receipts from outsourcing translation work and making payment of about Rs. 3 crores cannot be held good comparable with assessee engaged in ITES segment and needs to be excluded - Held, yes [Para 13] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : A company deriving significant portion of its receipts from outsourcing translation work and making payment of about Rs. 3 crores cannot be held good comparable with assessee engaged in ITES segment and needs to be excluded  TRANSFER PRICING : When missing of details relating to capacity underutilization adjustment resulted in observation of TPO that TP study of assessee has not made any such adjustment, then issue should be remanded to file of Assessing Officer/TPO for considering capacity underutilization adjustment in light of TP study and by requiring details, if any, from assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company engaged in relative position of things on earth's surface which include 3D mapping, Navigation maps, image processing, Cadastral mapping etc. cannot be compared with assessee providing services in ITES segment

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee rendered ITES to its AE - Whether company engaged in providing engineering design service which is a high end service in nature of KPO,cannot be treated as comparable - Held, yes - Whether company which had outsourced its ITES to third party vendors was incomparable - Held, yes - Whether since extraordinary event had impacted profitability of comparable company, it should be excluded from comparable list - Held, yes - Whether engineering design services could not be compared to IT enabled services - Held, yes [Paras 53 to 67][Matter remanded]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether where assessee was rendering ITES services to AE as captive service provider, a company which outsourced major portion of its work, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Para 15.3.2] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Employees Cost) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where assessee was rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which outsourced major portion of its work to third parties and thereby followed a different business model, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Para 11] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which outsourced major portion of its work to third parties and thereby followed a different business model, could not be accepted as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was rendering ITES services to its AE, a company having unreliable financial data, was not acceptable as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING: Where TPO made addition to assessee's ALP in respect of interest on loan availed from AE, in view of fact that computation of interest by TPO on basis of RBI ECB rate was flawed since interest was paid by assessee to AEs located in foreign countries, impugned addition was to be deleted

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITES)) - Assessment year 2012-13 - Assessee-company was engaged in providing Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) to its Associated Enterprises (AEs) - TPO selected certain companies as comparable to assessee - It was found that Tribunal in case of Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT in [2018] 97 taxmann.com 2 (Banglore-Trib.) had remanded matter as regards said comparables for examination and verification of issues raised by assessee of functional comparability and employees cost filter of 25 per cent at segmental level - Whether, in view of aforesaid, issue of comparability of said companies was to be remanded back to TPO for examination - Held, yes [Para 6.3.2] [Matter remanded]TRANSFER PRICING: In view of Tribunal's decision in Mobily Infotech India (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT in [2018] 97 taxmann.com 2 (Banglore-Trib.) issue of comparability of companies selected by TPO was to be remanded for examination and verification of issues raised by assessee of functional comparability and employees cost filter of 25 per cent at segmental level  TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was providing Information Technology Enabled Services to its AEs, a company having huge brand value was to be excluded from list of comaprables  TRANSFER PRICING: A company which had extraordinary events happened in relevant year under consideration such as acquisition of an Australian company which had effect on its profits was to be excluded from list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING: Where a company had 3 segments and benchmarking had been done only with one segment and it was not clear, how much of RPT expenses pertained to each of segments, matter was to be remanded  TRANSFER PRICING: Where a company was Knowledge Process Outsourcing (KPO) services provider but it was not predominantly a Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) company, was comparable to assessee providing Information Technology Enabled Services to its AEs  TRANSFER PRICING: Where DRP excluded a company from set of comparables, however, it was found that said company had only one segment, namely, Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) segment which was functionally comparable to assessee providing ITES facts.text:
The assessee-company was a wholly owned subsidiary of US company. It provided Research and Information Services and IT Support Services to its AE.

Operating Profit (OP)/Operating Cost (OC) was accepted as the Profit Level Indicator (PLI) by the TPO. However, out of 16 companies selected by the assessee as comparable companies, the TPO rejected 14 (including non-Indian companies). A final list of 8 comparable companies, including two companies chosen by the assessee was finally drawn up by the TPO proposing upward adjustment in respect of provision of IT Support Services and in respect of provision of Research and Information Services.

Disputes Resolution Panel (DRP) allowed part relief to the assessee.

By the impugned order. the Tribunal partly allowed the assessee's appeal and directed exclusion of four comparables, by applying stringent standards of comparability analysis to comparables selected under the Transaction Net Margin Method. Further, the Tribunal held concluding that nature of services provided by it under the R&I segment was in the nature of KPO services, whereas, according to assessee, it functioned more like a BPO.

On appeal:

The assessee-company was engaged in the business of software development services and ITES/BPO services. The assessee during the year under dispute provided such services only to its Associated Enterprise (AE). It had selected TNM Method as the most appropriate method and OP/TC as the profit level indicator for both the segments.

On reference, the TPO rejected the TP document of the assessee pointing out various defects and deficiencies. He undertook a search in the databases and computed the ALP of both the segments.

On the basis of transfer pricing adjustment computed by the TPO, the Assessing Officer passed the assessment order making certain additions.

The Commissioner (Appeals) dismissed the appeal of the assessee rejecting all its contentions.

The assessee objected to the following companies being treated as comparables in the software service segment:

(i)

Exensys Software Solutions Ltd.: The assessee submitted that not only the aforesaid company was involved in development of products but there was also an extraordinary event of merger during the relevant financial year.

(ii)

Thirdware Solutions Ltd.: The company was into development of product and involved in distribution activities. Therefore, it could not be treated as a comparable.

(iii)

Infosys Technologies Ltd.: The assessee contended that under no circumstances Infosys Technologies Ltd. could be treated as comparable to the assessee as it is a giant in the sector of software development and ITES having considerable brand value. The revenue, on the other hand, while strongly opposing contention of the assessee, submitted that the assessee itself in its own TP Study had selected Infosys Technologies Ltd. as a comparable.

The assessee had also sought exclusion of following comparable companies selected by the TPO in the ITES segment:

(i)

Vishal Information Technologies Ltd.: The company had outsourced a considerable part of its business to third party vendors. That was proved from the fact that only 2 per cent of the revenue was spent towards employee cost and there was huge vendor payment.

(ii)

Maple E Solutions Ltd.: The company could not be treated as comparable as the directors of the said company were found to be involved in fraud, hence financial results of the company could not be trusted as reliable.

(iii)

Wipro BPO Solutions Ltd.: WIPRO commands a premium in the pricing of its products and services due to goodwill, reputation and brand value. Therefore, it could not be compared to a risk mitigated captive service provider like the assessee.

Coral Hub Ltd.

This case was earlier included by the assessee in the list of comparables in the transfer pricing study by considering multiple-year data. However, when the TPO required the assessee to furnish data of comparables for the current year alone, the assessee requested for the exclusion of this case from the list of comparables. The revenue opposed this contention by urging that the assessee cannot be allowed to resile from its original stand. [Para 12.1] The legal objection taken by the revenue that the assessee should be prohibited from taking a stand contrary to the one which was taken at the stage of the TP study or during the course of proceedings before the authorities below cannot be accepted. It goes without saying that the object of assessment is to determine the income in respect of which the assessee is rightly chargeable to tax. As the income not originally offered for taxation, if otherwise chargeable, is required to be included in the total income, in the same breath, any income wrongly included in the total income, which is not otherwise chargeable, should be excluded. There can be no estoppel against the provisions of the Act. Extending this proposition further to the context of the transfer pricing, if the assessee fails to report an otherwise comparable case, then the TPO is obliged to include it in the list of comparables, and in the same manner, if the assessee wrongly reported an incomparable case as comparable in its TP study and then later on claims that it should be excluded then, there should be nothing to forbid the assessee from claiming so, provided the TPO is satisfied that the case so originally reported as comparable is, in fact, not comparable. [Para 12.2]

The material on record suggests that outsourcing charges of comparable constitute 90 per cent of the total operating cost in this case. On a specific query, the revenue admitted that our assessee is engaged in the business of doing activities at its own without any outsourcing. This crucial factor, having a greater bearing on the profitability, makes it distinguishable from the assessee. The Mumbai Bench of the Tribunal in the case of Asstt. CIT v. Hapag Lloyd Global Services (P.) Ltd. [IT Appeal No. 8499 (Mum.) of 2010, dated 28-2-2013] has held that Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. cannot be considered as comparable because of the overwhelming outsourcing activity carried out by it. This view was taken by relying on another order passed by the Mumbai Bench of the Tribunal in Asstt. CIT v. Maersk Global Service Center (India) (P.) Ltd. [2011] 133 ITD 543/16 taxmann.com 47. In the later case also, the Tribunal held that the case of Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. or Coral Hub Ltd. was not includible in the list of comparables because of major outsourcing. Since the facts of the instant case are on all fours with these two cases, it is opined that this case is required to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 12.3]

Cosmic Global Limited

From the material on record it is apparent that outsourcing charges of this case constitute 57.31 per cent of the total operating costs. This does not appear to be a valid reason for eliminating this case from the list of comparables. On going through the Annual accounts of Cosmic Global Limited, it is found that its total revenue from operations are at Rs.7.37 crore divided into three segments, namely, Medical transcription and consultancy services at Rs.9.90 lakhs, Translation charges at Rs.6.99 crore and Accounts BPO at Rs.27.76 lakhs. The assessee has made out a case that outsourcing activity carried out by this company constitutes 57 per cent of total expenses.

When one is examining the results of this company from the Accounts BPO segment alone, there is no need to examine the position under other segments. The entire outsourcing is confined to Translation charges paid at Rs.3.00 crore, which is strictly in the realm of the Translation segment, revenues from which are to the tune of Rs.6.99 crore. If this segment of Translation is not under consideration for deciding as to whether this case is comparable or not, one cannot take recourse to the figures which are relevant for segments other than accounts BPO. Thus it is held that this case cannot be excluded on the strength of outsourcing activity, which is alien to the relevant segment. [Para 13.2]

However, this case is found to incomparable on the alternative argument advanced by the assessee to the effect that total revenue of the Accounts BPO segment of Cosmic Global Limited is very low at Rs.27.76 lakhs. A captive unit cannot be compared with a giant case. As the segmental revenue of BPO segment of Cosmic Global Limited at Rs. 27.76 lakh is still on much lower side, this case is, therefore, directed to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 13.3]

ITES Segment

Comparables Manipal Digital Systems Pvt. Ltd., Domex E Data Pvt. Ltd., Eclerx Services Ltd. and MPS Ltd.

It is noted that all the above four comparables contested for exclusion under the ITES segment have been found to be engaged in high end KPO services and these comparables are full-fledged entrepreneurs. The TPO while analyzing the functions of the assessee under ITES segment has very categorically noted that assessee provides services to the insurance companies of the AE wherein it carries out filling up the claim entry form and patient registration, eligibility verification, claim submission and adjudication etc. under healthcare services under insurance and banking services, the assessee provides record processing services, KYC update services accounting services etc. It has been observed by the TPO that assessee neither directly pitches nor provides support in pitching work from customers. It is noted that assessee only provides assistance/advise from operations stand point to the solutions team in USA who in turn approaches the customer for work. It is opined that based on such limited functions of the assessee in ITES segment, all the above four comparables cannot be considered comparable with that of the assessee with high end activities. Further nothing contrary has been brought to notice by the revenue. Accordingly, the Assessing Officer/TPO is to be directed to exclude all the four comparables. [Para 6.3]

Comparable Accentia Technologies Ltd.

The Tribunal in the assessee's own case for assessment year 2011-12 has excluded this company from the list of comparables on the ground that 'Accentia' is engaged in diversified activity of medical transcription, medical coding, medical billing, etc. which are different from the activities of the assessee; which is in the nature of call centre and, therefore, functionally not comparable.

However, for the year under consideration, the DRP has examined the TP study of the assessee and has rendered a finding that the functions performed by the assessee in the case on hand are in the nature of Testing, Compatibility, Localization services and end user support services and, therefore, the services rendered by the assessee are a mix of both high end and low end services. In the light of the above factual finding rendered by the DRP, it may not be appropriate to apply the decision of the Tribunal, unless it is established that there is no change in the functional profile of the assessee in the year under consideration vis-à-vis the earlier years. Further, while the TPO has characterized the assessee as an ITES provider, but DRP had rendered the finding that the assessee provided a mix of ITES and KPO services. It would be appropriate to remand the issue of determining the functional profile of the assessee back to the file of the TPO for a fresh analysis, to evaluate the finding rendered by the DRP that the services rendered by the assessee are a mix of high end and low end services and also to evaluate the change in the functional profile of the assessee, if any, over the years and to then decide the comparability. [Para 7.3.2]

Comparable TCS E-serve Ltd.

From a perusal of the Annual Report of this company, 'TCS' for the year under consideration, it is seen that this company is an integral part of the Tata Consultancy Services strategy to build on its Full service Offerings ranging from IT Software development services to BPO services. This company offers BPO services in Banking, Financial Services and Insurance Services, the Operations include core business services, Analytics and Insights and support services for data and voice recording. [Para 8.3.1]

According to the assessee, the TPO rejected a company as comparable, for the earlier years on account of diversified activities and the assessee had mentioned that the services rendered by this company as KPO services, it has not brought out as to which of the services would come under Transaction Processing and which of the services rendered would constitute KPO services. Further, as mentioned earlier, the DRP has rendered a finding that the assessee provides a mix of high end and low end services. While this company 'TCS', has been excluded as a comparable for companies performing ITES services in the few other cases also, these judicial pronouncements pertain to earlier assessment years and the assessee in the case on hand has not demonstrated that all the reasons are equally applicable to this year also. [Para 8.3.2]

In the factual matrix of the case, an examination is necessary to decide whether the conditions/reasons on the basis of which this company was excluded in the earlier year are applicable to the fact situation prevailing in the assessment year under consideration.

Comparable BNR Udyog Ltd.

The contention of the assessee that this company, 'BNR', fails the RPT filter at the entity level has been countered by the TPO who has mentioned that while this company has three segments, the benchmarking has been done only with the Medical Transcription segment. The TPO has pointed out that while the entire Medical transcription segment is exported, the RPT are with domestic companies and, therefore, it could not have been with the Medical transcription segment. [Para 9.4.1]

The DRP in its order has further elaborated on the TPO's view that RPT expenses have been booked in the earlier year also when the Business support segment was in existence; which fact has been confirmed by this company is in response to information called for under section 133(6) of the Act. the rationale given by the DRP does not give any conclusive finding. If there was no Business Support Services Segment in the earlier year but RPT have been booked, it would mean that those RPT expenses pertain to the Medical transcription service segment in the earlier year. Since, in the current year under consideration, there are 2 segments, how much of the RPT pertains to each of the segments requires examination. [Para 9.4.2]

Comparable Company Infosys BPO:

Under the head 'Managements Discussion and Analysis' of this company, it has been stated that this company provides services to both horizontal and vertical focus areas. The Horizontal focus areas are Sourcing and Procurement (S & P), Customer Services (CS), Finance and Accounting (F & A), Legal Process Outsourcing (LPO), Sales and Fulfilment (S & F), Analytics (AT), Business Platform (BP), Business Transformation Services (BTS), Human Resources Outsourcing (HRO) and Technology Solution Optimization (TSO). The Vertical focus areas of services are Financial Services & Insurance (FSI) Manufacturing (MFG), Energy, Utilities Communication & Services (ECS) and Retail, Consumer Packaged Foods, Logistics & Life Services (RCL). From the above, it is clear that 'Infosys' offers a gamut of different and diversified services which cannot be compared with routine back office services provided by the assessee. In fact, it is mentioned in the annual report that the company 'Infosys' provides business process management services which are different from routine back office services. It is also to be seen that this company enjoys significant brand value and owns intangible assets which clearly establish that Infosys is different from the assessee in the case on hand. [Para 7.4.1]

This company has consistently been rejected as a comparable to companies rendering routine back office services in various judicial pronouncements of the Tribunal; including the two decisions cited by the assessee. In the case of CGI Informaiton Systems & Management Consultants (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2018] 94 taxmann.com 97 (Bangalore - Trib) for the Assessment Year 2012-13, cited by the assessee, this company 'Infosys' has been excluded from the list of comparables for the reason that it has brand value which had an impact on its pricing and margins. As the facts of the year under consideration are similar, the decision rendered in the earlier year would apply to the year under consideration as well. In this factual view of the matter, it is to be held that Infosys BPO, stands on a totally different footing from a company engaged in rendering routine back office ITES; being both functionally different and having brand value and, therefore, is to be excluded from the final set of comparables. [Para 7.4.2]

Comparable Company Microland:

It is to be seen that the services rendered by company 'Microland' under Infrastructure Management services are Server Management, Database Management, storage management, Archival Management, Network Management, etc., which has been classified as different from the back office processing services rendered by companies like the assessee in the case on hand. In view of this, there is no basis for the TPO to contend that the aforesaid services rendered by 'Microland' are ITES, when the company itself has classified these services as different from ITES and characterized the same as a different business segment. In these factual circumstances, contention of the assessee that the Infrastructure Management services segment of 'Microland' is different and distinct with ITES as has been classified by the company in its annual report for the year under consideration is to be accepted. It is also to be observed that the TPO himself has reached the same conclusion in the subsequent assessment year 2015-16; that the Infrastructure segment services segment is not comparable to ITES. [Para 8.4.3]

The annual report of 'Microland' for the year under consideration, the segmental details of the two business segments are provided from which it is seen that out of the total revenue of Rs. 34.471 lakhs, the revenue from ITES segment is Rs. 1959 lakhs; which is 5.68 per cent of the total revenue. As, it is already been concluded that the infrastructure services segment is a different business segment not comparable to ITES rendered; this company, 'Microland' fails the filter adopted by the TPO that companies whose service income is less than 75 per cent of total operating revenue are to be excluded. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, as discussed above, and in view of the above factual findings, company Microland is to be excluded from the final set of comparables in the case on hand. [Para 8.4.4]

Comparable Company Informed Technologies:

The nature of services rendered by the assessee to non-AEs broadly comprised of customer care and technical support, viz., payroll, recruitment, IT support etc. The business operations of the assessee are divided into various operational processes that it performs for its customers (AE's and non - AE's). While processes carried out for the AE and non-AE may differ, the fundamental functions performed by the assessee under each of these processes are the same and fall under the category of ITeS Industry. These aspects were never disputed by the TPO/AO at any stage. In fact, the TPO/AO simply stated that the nature of services performed in AE segment are totally different from nature of services in non-AE segment. But how the services are fundamentally different has not been demonstrated by the Assessing Officer. In fact, in broader context the services rendered to AE and non-AE were that of customer care and technical support, and thus, rejecting the internal TNMM on this ground was not valid as internal TNMM is the method which makes it easy to find comparable companies and reasonably determine the arm's length nature of related as well as unrelated transactions. Besides this the TPO/AO has also rejected internal TNMM on the ground that there were no audited segments maintained. But at the same time, the TPO/AO has not pointed out any discrepancy related to segmental analysis based on valid allocation keys furnished by the assessee in its TP study. Therefore, these two aspects cannot be valid for rejecting the internal TNMM. The DRP was not correct in considering the services/scope of work from the agreement entered into by the assessee with its AE for 'procurement of IT Services' and comparing the same with the back-end ITeS services provided by the assessee to AEs. In the present case, best suited method is internal TNMM. The financial data pertaining to internal segmentation is more reliable and accurate, as compared to financial data of external comparable companies, therefore, it will be appropriate to apply internal benchmarking analysis over external benchmarking analysis. The "OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations" highlight the preference of internal comparables over external comparables. In fact, the United Nations Practical Manual on Transfer Pricing for Developing Countries, released in 2013 (UN manual) also provides that TNMM is less dependent on product comparability because net margins are less influenced by differences in products and functions, as compared to other methods like CUP. Therefore, the TPO/AO is directed adopt internal TNMM for benchmarking provision of ITeS. [Para 10]

The assessee is seeking exclusion of three comparables from the list of 28 comparables considered by the TPO/AO. Comparable Global Ltd.

The assessee has sought exclusion of this comparable company mainly on the ground that it outsources most of its work which is 57.31 per cent as compared to the assessee which is only 2.5 per cent and employee cost of this company is lower. Though this is fairly a vital factor vitiating the comparability, however, the assessee could not give any rebuttal or any cogent reasons as to why this comparable company was selected and chosen by the assessee after carrying out FAR analysis not only in earlier years, but also in subsequent assessment years i.e. 2010-11 and 2011-12 again on carrying same FAR analysis. It is only in this year that assessee is seeking exclusion on the ground that it has a different business model. Such pick and choose of comparables every year according to the suitability of the margin definitely amounts to cherry picking. The assessee has not demonstrated that in earlier years and subsequent years the business model of Cosmic Global Ltd. is different, i.e., it does not outsource its substantial work. No doubt assessee can object to inclusion or exclusion of a comparable company contrary to its TP Study Report by citing cogent grounds and pointing out the factors vitiating the comparability and TPO has to examine these comparability factors on merits, but when assessee consistently adopts any comparable company and too after FAR scrutiny then onus is very heavy upon the assessee to substantiate that the material factors in the relevant year are different from the years when it seeks to take contrary stand in a particular year. The assessee has been unable to point out the material factors for distinction sought in this year was not permeating in the earlier years or in the subsequent years. This inconsistent approach cannot be permitted as it can lead to falling in the realm of whims of suitability of assessee. Had it been the case where material facts were different in this year and the comparable has been selected on some incorrect analysis in the earlier year or at the time of TP study, then definitely there cannot be any estoppel for objecting to for exclusion, but such material facts and incorrect approach has to be demonstrated which has not been done in this year. This inconsistency is further accentuated by the fact that this comparable continues to be part of assessee's comparable in subsequent years. Thus, assessee cannot be allowed to resort to such cherry picking. Accordingly, the action of the TPO in including Cosmic Global Ltd. as comparable following rule of consistency is upheld. [Para 15.3]

Comparable Genesys International

The view point of the authorities in forcefully including a company in the list of comparables simply on the ground that since the assessee initially voluntarily treated it as comparable, now it cannot resile, cannot be appreciated. The substance of the matter is to consider and decide the comparability of a company with the assessee on merits rather than harping on an inadvertent mistake committed by the assessee in this regard. If an assessee wrongly includes a company in the list of comparables and then puts up a case before the TPO that this company is, in fact, not comparable citing the reasons for its stand, the TPO is obliged to reject the contention under due process of law after successfully meeting with the objections so raised by the assessee. It cannot be a one sided wind blow. There can be no estoppel against the inclusion of correct companies in the tally of comparables. If one has to go strictly with the assessee's list of comparables by not accepting the contention for the exclusion of a particular company after proper evaluation, then, there ought to be complete acceptance of the assessee's version as regards the comparability of all other companies as well. There cannot be simultaneous approbate and reprobate. As the position is not so and TPO is fully empowered to examine and evaluate each and every company included by the assessee in its list of comparables from the angle of its actual comparability, in the like manner, the TPO should also examine the assessee's contention of incomparability of a company wrongly included by it in the list of comparables, if argued. [Para 13]

It can be seen that Genesys International falls under the caption 'Geographic Information System Services.' There can be no comparison of the services carried out by this company with those rendered by the assessee to its AEs. It was contention of the assessee-company that VITL had employee-cost at 1.38 per cent of its revenue when compared to that of the assessee-company which was at 52.12 per cent. Thus, the VITL could not be considered as comparable company and was to be excluded from the list of comparable companies. It was also an alternate contention of the assessee that VITL owned valuable intangible when compared to the assessee-company. Hence, the said company had to be excluded. The assessee-company itself agreed before the TPO that VITL was a comparable company offering IT enabled services and this company was an extension of one Indian company, having agreed so it was not correct on the part of the assessee-company to raise a new plea that the VITL had to pay low wages as compared to the assessee-company. It appeared that the VITL had outsourced the manpower and the cost of outsourcing appeared to have been included in the other heads of the expenditure instead of wages-employee cost. Moreover, the intangibles would not materially affect the price or profit earning. By outsourcing the manpower, the VITL would have incurred more cost compared to the assessee-company, thus resulting in lesser operating profit. But, having considering the findings of the TPO, it was found that the intangibles or outsourcing the manpower would not materially affect the price or profit margin. No two comparable companies can be replicas of each other. The application of rule 10B should be carried out and judged not with technical rigor, but on a broader prospective. In this view of the matter, there was no infirmity in the order of the Commissioner (Appeals) in confirming the action of the TPO by selecting the VITL as comparable company. [Para 36]

Another issue was as to whether the TPO was correct in selecting 'W' BPO having turnover of 20 times more than the assessee-company as comparable or not. It was found that this issue was covered in favour of the assessee by the decision of Delhi ITAT in the case of Agnity India Technologies (P.) Ltd [IT Appeal No. 3856/Delhi/2010]. The 'W' BPO was not at all comparable as the assessee-company was pigmy compared to giant 'W'. Turnover of 'W' BPO was 20 times more than the assessee-company. Hence, the assessee-company was not comparable with 'W' BPO, the reasoning being that the latter was a giant company having 20 times more turnover than the assessee-company. In view of this, based on the facts and the circumstances of the case, and following the decision of Delhi Bench of ITAT in the aforesaid case, it was opined that 'W' BPO should be excluded from the list of comparable companies. The assessee clearly demonstrated that ASL had only transaction with Apex Data in purchasing of fixed assets. Relevant papers were placed on record by the assessee. In view of this matter, it was found that there was no controlled transaction between the ASL and Apex Data. Thus, no materially significant related party transactions existed section 92A(2)(i) clearly deals with manufacturing of goods and articles and not with provision of services. There is an apparent conflict between the description of services as stated by the assessee and as recorded in the order of the TPO. [Para 50]

In an attempt to ascertain the correct nature of services, the Master Services Agreement entered into by the assessee with McKinsey is referred to. It is a common Agreement between the assessee and McKinsey for providing both the 'Research and information services' and also 'IT support services'. [Para 51]

It is deducible that the nature of service covered under the 'IT Support services' segment are '(a) Develop, maintain and service the software … and (b) Knowledge management systems and infrastructure issues which would encompass infrastructure support, application support, application operations group and survey development center and such other services as may be requested from time to time'. Thus, it is overt that there is a vast difference about the nature of services as argued by the assessee under this segment as that of 'help desk services', being BPO; and what is coming out from the Master Services Agreement as also inclusive of 'Knowledge management systems and infrastructure issues which would encompass infrastructure support, application support, application operations group and survey development center', which are KPO in nature. It comes out that employees of assessee consist of 17 IT Analysts, apart from Fast Regional Manager- Asia Pac, 2 Operations Managers, Technology Line Leader, Team Leader, and only 1 Team Assistant. In view of the apparent conflict in what the assessee is stating and what is prima facie coming out from record, without there being any material to show the exact nature of services, the comparability or otherwise of the companies challenged before the Tribunal cannot be decided. Though the TPO has considered only segmental data relating to ITES services, however, there is no denial that this company is having significant investment in the business acquisition as well as engaged in the innovation activities of various fields including technology innovation, process innovation and delivery innovation.
